knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structured Large-Residual Correction Method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)^T:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|R(x)\|_2^2\). Put \(J(x)=R'(x)\) and \(S(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x)\nabla^2r_i(x)\), so \(\nabla^2f(x)=J(x)^TJ(x)+S(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear least squares, especially nonzero-residual regimes in which the second Hessian term is not negligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A large-residual correction method is a least-squares iteration that retains the Gauss–Newton term \(J_k^TJ_k\) and augments it with a symmetric correction \(S_k\approx S(x_k)\). Its step is obtained from a line-search or trust-region quadratic model \[m_k(p)=f(x_k)+\nabla f(x_k)^Tp+\tfrac12p^T(J_k^TJ_k+S_k)p.\] A structured secant instance requires, for \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \[S_{k+1}s_k=y_k^{\sharp},\qquad y_k^{\sharp}=J_{k+1}^TR_{k+1}-J_k^TR_{k+1},\] together with symmetry and an update-selection rule such as least change. The family also includes hybrids that use a Gauss–Newton model when it predicts well and activate the correction when residual curvature is significant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large-residual correction method augments the Gauss–Newton Hessian term with a symmetric approximation to the residual-weighted sum of the component Hessians. A structured secant version updates that correction through the stated residual-specific secant equation and uses the resulting matrix in a line-search or trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=J_k^TJ_k+S_k\) with \(S_k\approx\sum_i r_i(x_k)\nabla^2r_i(x_k)\), and a structured update may impose \(S_{k+1}s_k=J_{k+1}^TR_{k+1}-J_k^TR_{k+1}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(S_k=S(x_k)\), the model has the exact Hessian \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\).
special_cases_latex: Setting \(S_k=0\) gives the Gauss–Newton model.
At a zero-residual solution \(R(x_*)=0\), the exact correction satisfies \(S(x_*)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The correction targets curvature omitted by Gauss–Newton without discarding the explicitly available matrix \(J_k^TJ_k\).
boundary_notes: A large numerical value of \(\|R(x_k)\|\) alone is not the definition; the relevant issue is the significance of \(S(x)\) in the local Hessian.
The definition does not require the corrected matrix to be positive definite; globalization must handle indefiniteness if it occurs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separable Nonlinear Least-Squares Problem and Method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(a\in\mathbb R^p\) denote linear parameters and \(z\in\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) nonlinear parameters. Let \(A:\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R^{m\times p}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and define \(R(a,z)=A(z)a-b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional least squares that is linear in one parameter block and nonlinear in another; unconstrained linear variables are used in the canonical form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separable nonlinear least-squares problem has the form \[\min_{a\in\mathbb R^p,\,z\in\mathcal Z}\;F(a,z)=\tfrac12\|A(z)a-b\|_2^2.\] A separable least-squares method is an iteration that resolves the linear block by linear least squares for fixed \(z\), exactly or to a declared tolerance, and updates the nonlinear block using the resulting reduced or coupled model. Define \(a(z)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a}\|A(z)a-b\|_2\) and \(\phi(z)=\tfrac12\|A(z)a(z)-b\|_2^2\). Exact elimination is permitted whenever the attained residual norm is independent of the chosen minimizer \(a(z)\), as it is for ordinary linear least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable least-squares problem is linear in one parameter block and nonlinear in another. A separable method exploits this structure by solving the linear least-squares subproblem for each nonlinear parameter value and then treating either the resulting reduced objective or an equivalent coupled system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(a,z)=\tfrac12\|A(z)a-b\|_2^2\), with the linear block resolved by \(a(z)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_a\|A(z)a-b\|_2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The residual may be written componentwise as \(r_i(a,z)=\sum_{j=1}^pA_{ij}(z)a_j-b_i\).
If \(A(z)\) has full column rank, \(a(z)=(A(z)^TA(z))^{-1}A(z)^Tb\).
special_cases_latex: With \(q=0\), the problem is ordinary linear least squares.
With \(p=0\), no separable linear block remains.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact elimination reduces the nonlinear search dimension from \(p+q\) to \(q\).
No initial estimate for the eliminated linear parameters is required.
boundary_notes: Partial separability as a sum of element functions is a different structure from linear–nonlinear parameter separability.
Rank-deficient linear subproblems may have nonunique coefficients even though their fitted vector and residual norm are unique.

notation.meaning: Parameter block entering the residual linearly.
Parameter block entering the design matrix nonlinearly.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable projection solves the linear coefficients exactly for each nonlinear parameter and optimizes only the resulting projected residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{a\in\mathbb{R}^p,\,z\in\mathbb{R}^q}\tfrac12\lVert A(z)a-b\rVert_2^2.\] For each admissible \(z\), compute \(a(z)=A(z)^\dagger b\) and the projected residual \(\rho(z)=(I-A(z)A(z)^\dagger)b\). Apply a nonlinear least-squares method to \(\phi(z)=\tfrac12\lVert\rho(z)\rVert_2^2\), using derivatives of the projector on regions of constant rank. After a stopping test for the reduced problem is met at \(z_*\), return \((a(z_*),z_*)\). Every global minimizer of the reduced problem, paired with its least-norm eliminated coefficient, is a global minimizer of the original separable problem.
assumptions_latex: The rank of \(A(z)\) is locally constant wherever reduced derivatives are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimizing \(\phi(z)\) is equivalent in optimal value to minimizing the original separable least-squares objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of linear coefficients in separable nonlinear least squares.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and elimination principle match variable projection. Continuity of A(z) and locally constant rank are insufficient for the instruction to use projector derivatives; A must have the corresponding differentiability. A dedicated variable-projection source is also needed for the reduced derivative construction and constant-rank conditions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variable Projection for Separable Least Squares
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A:\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(F(a,z)=\tfrac12\|A(z)a-b\|_2^2\). Let \(A(z)^\dagger\) be the Moore–Penrose inverse and \(P_{A(z)}=A(z)A(z)^\dagger\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact projection for unregularized Euclidean separable least squares; smooth reduced derivatives require locally constant rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The variable-projection reduction eliminates the linear coefficients by \[a(z)=A(z)^\dagger b,\qquad r_{\mathrm{vp}}(z)=A(z)a(z)-b=-(I-P_{A(z)})b,\] and defines the reduced objective \[\phi(z)=\tfrac12\|r_{\mathrm{vp}}(z)\|_2^2=\tfrac12\|(I-P_{A(z)})b\|_2^2.\] A variable-projection method applies a nonlinear least-squares, line-search, or trust-region iteration to \(\phi\), recomputing an optimal linear coefficient vector at each trial \(z\). A returned full-space point is \((a(z),z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable projection solves the linear least-squares block at every nonlinear parameter value, substitutes that solution into the residual, and optimizes the norm of the component of the data orthogonal to the range of the current design matrix.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For each fixed \(z\), \(A(z)^T(A(z)a(z)-b)=0\).
If \(A(z)\) has full column rank, \(P_{A(z)}=A(z)(A(z)^TA(z))^{-1}A(z)^T\).
special_cases_latex: If \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A(z))\), then \(\phi(z)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every global minimizer of the reduced problem, paired with a linear least-squares minimizer, is a global minimizer of the original separable problem.
The nonlinear iteration has dimension \(q\) rather than \(p+q\).
boundary_notes: At rank changes, the projector and reduced residual need not be differentiable even when \(A(z)\) is smooth.
This slot excludes regularization of the eliminated coefficients.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose inverse of the design matrix.
Orthogonal projector onto the range of A(z).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled Block Resolution in Separable Least Squares
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(a,z)=\tfrac12\|A(z)a-b\|_2^2\), with \(a\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(z\in\mathbb R^q\). At \((a_k,z_k)\), let the linearized residual be \(r_k+A_kp_a+G_kp_z\), where \(A_k=A(z_k)\) and \(G_k=D_z(A(z)a)|_{(a_k,z_k)}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth separable least squares; the definition covers simultaneous elimination of the linearized linear-parameter step rather than exact nonlinear variable projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separable coupling-resolution method computes a coupled model step \((p_a,p_z)\) by first resolving the linear block in \[\min_{p_a,p_z}\;\tfrac12\|r_k+A_kp_a+G_kp_z\|_2^2+\mathcal R_k(p_a,p_z),\] where \(\mathcal R_k\) is a declared regularization or trust-region term. In the unregularized case, for every candidate \(p_z\), it selects \[p_a(p_z)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p_a}\|r_k+A_kp_a+G_kp_z\|_2\] and solves the induced projected model in \(p_z\). The defining feature is resolution of the coupling inside the local step model; it does not require exact elimination of \(a\) from the original nonlinear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable coupling-resolution method linearizes the jointly dependent residual and eliminates or solves the linear-parameter step inside that local model. This differs from exact variable projection, which eliminates the linear parameters from the original objective at every nonlinear parameter value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_a(p_z)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p_a}\|r_k+A_kp_a+G_kp_z\|_2\), followed by optimization of the resulting model over \(p_z\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Without regularization, the resolved step satisfies \(A_k^T(r_k+A_kp_a(p_z)+G_kp_z)=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(G_k=0\), the step reduces to a linear least-squares correction in \(a\).
immediate_consequences_latex: With full column rank of \(A_k\), the linearized coefficient step is unique for every \(p_z\).
boundary_notes: The node title does not identify a universally standardized named method family.
No inspected source precisely defines this local coupling-resolution class.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the residual with respect to the nonlinear parameter block at the current pair.

Alternating Least-Squares Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating least squares minimizes one parameter block at a time; exact block solves make the objective nonincreasing but do not ensure global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_B)=\tfrac12\lVert r(x_1,\ldots,x_B)\rVert_2^2\) on \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_B\). Starting from \(x^0\), one sweep computes, for \(b=1,\ldots,B\), \[x_b^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X_b}F(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{b-1}^{k+1},u,x_{b+1}^{k},\ldots,x_B^{k}).\] Stop after a sweep when the objective decrease or a block-stationarity measure is below tolerance, and return the last block vector. Exact block minimization gives \(F(x^{k+1})\leq F(x^k)\), but without additional regularity the method guarantees neither convergence to a joint minimizer nor uniqueness of the limit.
assumptions_latex: Each block feasible set \(X_b\) is nonempty.
Every displayed block subproblem attains a minimizer.
The same deterministic tie-breaking rule is used when a block minimizer is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective values generated by exact cyclic block minimization are nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic exact block minimization for multiblock least-squares objectives.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cyclic exact-block algorithm and monotonicity conclusion fit the terminal container and are mathematically plausible. The broader statement about absent joint-minimizer convergence and limit uniqueness is nontrivial and has no cited source or locator. A block-coordinate or alternating least-squares reference is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Elimination Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial elimination solves one parameter block exactly, optimizes the reduced value function, and reconstructs the eliminated block afterward.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(u,v)=	frac12\lVert r(u,v)Vert^2\) on \(U	imes V\). Suppose that, for each \(v\in V\), an inner solver returns \(u(v)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in U}F(u,v)\). Define the reduced objective \(\varphi(v)=F(u(v),v)=\min_{u\in U}F(u,v)\), optimize \(\varphi\) over \(V\), and return \((u(v_*),v_*)\). If the inner minimizer is locally unique, interior, and satisfies \(
abla_{uu}^2F(u(v),v)\succ0\), then \[
abla\varphi(v)=
abla_vF(u(v),v).\] Moreover, any global minimizer \(v_*\) of \(\varphi\) produces a global minimizer of \(F\).
assumptions_latex: For every considered \(v\), the inner minimization over \(U\) attains its minimum.
For the gradient identity, the inner minimizer is locally unique and interior.
For the gradient identity, \(F\) is twice continuously differentiable and its inner Hessian is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact partial elimination preserves the global optimal value and yields the stated envelope gradient under regularity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of a selected parameter block before reduced optimization.

notation.meaning: selected exact minimizer of the eliminated block
feasible sets of eliminated and retained variables

The envelope-gradient statement also requires an appropriate open-domain or interior condition for the retained variable v, in addition to the stated inner regularity. A directly relevant source is needed before choosing the corrected hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the residual xy−1, alternating exact block solves can stay at the origin even though points with xy=1 attain zero residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the coupled least-squares objective \[F(x,y)=\tfrac12(xy-1)^2\] on \(\mathbb{R}^2\). At \((x,y)=(0,0)\), fixing \(y=0\) makes \(F(x,0)=\tfrac12\) for every \(x\), and fixing \(x=0\) makes \(F(0,y)=\tfrac12\) for every \(y\). Thus an alternating least-squares scheme whose tie rule retains the current coordinate remains forever at \((0,0)\). Nevertheless, every point satisfying \(xy=1\) has objective value zero. Hence monotone exact block minimization can stall at a coordinatewise minimizer that is not a local or global minimizer when coupling destroys uniqueness and blockwise curvature.
assumptions_latex: Alternating minimization solves each one-coordinate subproblem exactly.
When a block subproblem has multiple minimizers, the tie rule retains the current coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact alternating least squares may stagnate away from every joint minimizer when block minimizers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise optimality can fail to imply joint least-squares optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Variable Projection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the regularized linear variables exactly, optimize the resulting reduced objective over nonlinear variables, and recover the linear component at the final nonlinear iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given residuals affine in the linear variable, define \(r(y,z)=A(y)z-b\) and \(\Phi(y,z)=\tfrac12\lVert r(y,z)\rVert_2^2+\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\lVert Lz\rVert_2^2\), where \(\lambda>0\). For each outer iterate \(y_k\), compute \(z_k\) as the unique solution of \((A(y_k)^\top A(y_k)+\lambda L^\top L)z=A(y_k)^\top b\). Form the reduced objective \(\psi(y)=\Phi(y,z_\lambda(y))\), choose a descent or trust-region step \(s_k\) from a model of \(\psi\), and set \(y_{k+1}=y_k+s_k\). Stop when the reduced first-order residual is below tolerance; output \((y_k,z_\lambda(y_k))\).
assumptions_latex: \(A(y)^\top A(y)+\lambda L^\top L\) is positive definite at every evaluated \(y\).
The reduced-model step is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is a regularized variable-projection method for minimizing \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tikhonov-regularized elimination of linear variables in separable nonlinear least squares.

notation.meaning: Unique regularized linear least-squares minimizer at fixed y.

The dimensions and roles of b and L are also not fully introduced. A source specifically covering regularized variable projection is required before selecting the precise formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratically Regularized Variable Projection
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A:\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(L\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times p}\), and \(\lambda>0\). Define \(F_\lambda(a,z)=\tfrac12\|A(z)a-b\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|La\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tikhonov regularization of the linear parameter block in finite-dimensional separable least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Regularized variable projection eliminates \(a\) through \[a_\lambda(z)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{\tfrac12\|A(z)a-b\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|La\|_2^2\right\}\] and defines \[\phi_\lambda(z)=\tfrac12\|A(z)a_\lambda(z)-b\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|La_\lambda(z)\|_2^2.\] If \(A(z)^TA(z)+\lambda L^TL\) is nonsingular, then \(a_\lambda(z)=(A(z)^TA(z)+\lambda L^TL)^{-1}A(z)^Tb\). A regularized variable-projection method iterates on \(z\) using this reduced objective and recovers the linear block from \(a_\lambda(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized variable projection minimizes a penalized linear least-squares subproblem for every nonlinear parameter value, substitutes its solution into the full penalized objective, and optimizes the resulting reduced function over the nonlinear variables.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inner problem equals ordinary least squares for the augmented system \(\left[\begin{smallmatrix}A(z)\\\sqrt\lambda L\end{smallmatrix}\right]a\approx\left[\begin{smallmatrix}b\\0\end{smallmatrix}\right]\).
special_cases_latex: For \(L=I\), the inner solve is ridge-regularized least squares.
Formally setting \(\lambda=0\) recovers unregularized variable projection when the unregularized inner problem is well posed.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\ker A(z)\cap\ker L=\{0\}\), the inner minimizer is unique.
boundary_notes: Nonsmooth penalties on \(a\), constraints on \(a\), and regularization depending jointly on \((a,z)\) require distinct reduced formulations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonquadratic Robust Residual Objective and Method Family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)^T:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(\sigma_i>0\), and let \(\rho_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be loss functions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise robust residual objectives in finite dimensions; the losses may be smooth or nonsmooth and convex or nonconvex, provided the chosen algorithm declares the regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonquadratic robust residual problem is \[\min_{x\in\mathcal D}\;F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i\!\left(\frac{r_i(x)}{\sigma_i}\right),\] where at least one \(\rho_i\) is not a positive quadratic on all of \(\mathbb R\), and large arguments receive less than quadratic marginal influence in the robust case. A robust residual method is any iteration whose model, generalized gradient, or reweighting rule is constructed from this declared \(F\), rather than from the unqualified least-squares objective \(\tfrac12\|R(x)\|_2^2\). For differentiable losses, \[\nabla F(x)=J(x)^TD_\sigma^{-1}\psi(D_\sigma^{-1}R(x)),\qquad \psi_i=\rho_i',\] with componentwise evaluation of \(\psi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family minimizes a sum of declared nonquadratic losses of scaled residual components. Robust losses reduce the marginal influence of sufficiently large residuals. Methods in the family must construct their local equations or models from this objective, not silently replace it by ordinary least squares.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)=\sum_i\rho_i(r_i(x)/\sigma_i)\), with at least one globally nonquadratic loss and, in the differentiable case, \(\nabla F(x)=J(x)^TD_\sigma^{-1}\psi(D_\sigma^{-1}R(x))\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With a vector loss \(\rho:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\), the objective is \(F(x)=\rho(R(x))\); the componentwise form is the separable-loss specialization.
special_cases_latex: Huber loss is quadratic near zero and linear in magnitude beyond its threshold.
A bounded redescending loss, such as the Beaton–Tukey loss, yields vanishing influence beyond its cutoff.
immediate_consequences_latex: Ordinary least squares is recovered when every \(\rho_i(t)=t^2/2\), but then the objective is not nonquadratic.
boundary_notes: Robustness is not guaranteed merely by using a nonquadratic loss; its influence or tail behavior must be specified.
Redescending losses are generally nonconvex and may have multiple stationary points.

notation.meaning: Influence function, equal to the derivative of the ith loss where differentiable.
Diagonal matrix of positive residual scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteratively Reweighted Least-Squares Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly convert a robust residual objective into a weighted least-squares model, solve it, and globalize or damp the resulting step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(r_i(x))\), initialize \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\), assign \(w_i^k=\rho_i'(r_i(x_k))/r_i(x_k)\) when \(r_i(x_k)\ne0\), using the continuous nonnegative extension at zero. Compute \(s_k\) by minimizing \(\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m w_i^k(r_i(x_k)+\nabla r_i(x_k)^\top s)^2+\tfrac{\mu_k}{2}\lVert s\rVert_2^2\), where \(\mu_k\ge0\), and accept or damp the step according to decrease in \(F\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k s_k\). Stop when the robust gradient or step norm meets its tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each loss \(\rho_i\) is differentiable and yields nonnegative finite weights.
The regularized weighted subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed iteration defines the smooth-loss iteratively reweighted least-squares family.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth robust-loss IRLS with weights derived from the loss derivative.

notation.meaning: Weight assigned to residual i at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)^T:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^m\), scales \(\sigma_i>0\), and differentiable even losses \(\rho_i\) with influence functions \(\psi_i=\rho_i'\). Put \(t_i(x)=r_i(x)/\sigma_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component-separable differentiable M-estimation; zero residuals require a declared continuous extension of the weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An iteratively reweighted least-squares method for \(F(x)=\sum_i\rho_i(t_i(x))\) defines at iterate \(x_k\) nonnegative weights \[w_i^{(k)}=\begin{cases}\psi_i(t_i(x_k))/t_i(x_k),&t_i(x_k)\ne0,\\ \lim_{t\to0}\psi_i(t)/t,&t_i(x_k)=0,\end{cases}\] whenever these quantities exist, and computes \(x_{k+1}\) by solving or approximately solving the weighted nonlinear least-squares surrogate \[\min_{x\in\mathcal D}\;Q_k(x)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m w_i^{(k)}\left(\frac{r_i(x)}{\sigma_i}\right)^2,\] possibly with damping, a trust region, or proximal regularization. The family is distinguished by recomputation of residual-dependent weights between least-squares subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: IRLS alternates between calculating weights from the current scaled residuals and solving a weighted least-squares problem. For a differentiable M-loss, the canonical weight is its influence divided by the residual, with a continuous value assigned at zero.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed weights, \(Q_k(x)=\tfrac12\|W_k^{1/2}D_\sigma^{-1}R(x)\|_2^2\).
special_cases_latex: For quadratic loss, every weight is constant and IRLS reduces to a single weighted least-squares model family.
For Huber loss, \(w(t)=1\) inside the threshold and is proportional to \(1/|t|\) outside it.
immediate_consequences_latex: The weighted normal-equation gradient at \(x_k\) matches the robust-objective gradient when the stated weight identity is used.
boundary_notes: Negative weights do not define an ordinary weighted least-squares subproblem and are excluded here.
The definition alone does not assert descent or convergence for nonconvex losses.
No inspected source gives the exact IRLS iteration and zero-residual convention.

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix containing the current nonnegative residual weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares
Robust Gauss–Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use robust-loss weights in a Gauss–Newton system, globalize the computed direction, and stop when the weighted first-order residual is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(r_i(x))\). At \(x_k\), form \(r_k=r(x_k)\), \(J_k=J_r(x_k)\), and diagonal \(W_k\) with \((W_k)_{ii}=\rho_i'(r_{k,i})/r_{k,i}\), continuously extended at zero. Compute \(s_k\) from \((J_k^\top W_kJ_k+\mu_k I)s_k=-J_k^\top W_kr_k\), with \(\mu_k\ge0\). Choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) by a line-search or trust-region acceptance test for \(F\), then set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ks_k\). Terminate when \(\lVert J_k^\top W_kr_k\rVert\) is below tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The loss-derived weights are finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is a robust Gauss–Newton method with loss-dependent curvature approximation \(J_k^\top W_kJ_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauss–Newton linearization for differentiable robust sums of scalar residual losses.

notation.meaning: Residual Jacobian at the current iterate.
Regularization parameter ensuring a solvable model system.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the terminal container, but no evidence supports this particular weight formula, curvature approximation, regularization, and globalization combination. A source must also establish the conditions under which the continuous zero-residual weight is finite and nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust Gauss–Newton Step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(r_i(x)/\sigma_i)\), let \(J_k=R'(x_k)\), and suppose \(w_i^{(k)}=\psi_i(t_i(x_k))/t_i(x_k)\geq0\) is defined with a continuous convention at zero. Let \(D_\sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth residual maps with differentiable component losses and nonnegative local weights; globalization is optional but must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A robust Gauss–Newton method forms \[g_k=J_k^TD_\sigma^{-1}\psi(D_\sigma^{-1}R_k),\qquad B_k=J_k^TD_\sigma^{-1}W_kD_\sigma^{-1}J_k,\] and selects a step from the weighted Gauss–Newton model \[m_k(p)=F(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp.\] An undamped step satisfies \(B_kp_k=-g_k\) when this system is solvable; damped or trust-region variants replace it by a regularized system or constrained model minimization. The method is robust only relative to the declared losses and scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust Gauss–Newton replaces the ordinary least-squares normal matrix by a residual-weighted normal matrix derived from a robust loss. It then solves the corresponding quadratic model, optionally with damping or a trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=J_k^TD_\sigma^{-1}W_kD_\sigma^{-1}J_k\) and an undamped robust Gauss–Newton step satisfies \(B_kp_k=-J_k^TD_\sigma^{-1}\psi(D_\sigma^{-1}R_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The step is a Gauss–Newton step for the locally weighted residual \(W_k^{1/2}D_\sigma^{-1}(R_k+J_kp)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\rho_i(t)=t^2/2\), \(W_k=I\) and the ordinary scaled Gauss–Newton method is recovered.
immediate_consequences_latex: If all weights are nonnegative, \(B_k\) is positive semidefinite.
Zero weights suppress the corresponding residual rows in the local curvature model.
boundary_notes: Indefinite exact robust Hessian terms involving derivatives of the weights are omitted, as in the Gauss–Newton approximation.
No inspected locator states this combined robust Gauss–Newton construction exactly.

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix of robust weights evaluated at the current residual.

review_flags: Separate inspected sources cover robust losses and ordinary Gauss–Newton, but neither locator supports the exact combined definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Gauss–Newton Step
Other-Norm Residual Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a residual norm other than the Euclidean norm by solving norm-matched linearized subproblems within a globalization mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a residual map \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and a norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal R}\), minimize \(F(x)=\lVert r(x)\rVert_{\mathcal R}\). At \(x_k\), construct the linearized residual model \(r(x_k)+J_k s\) and compute \(s_k\) as a minimizer of \(\lVert r(x_k)+J_ks\rVert_{\mathcal R}\) over \(\lVert s\rVert_2\le\Delta_k\), or an accuracy-controlled approximation thereof. Accept \(x_k+s_k\) when actual reduction in \(F\) is commensurate with predicted reduction; otherwise reduce \(\Delta_k\). Stop using a norm-appropriate stationarity measure and return the accepted iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is continuously differentiable on an open set containing the iterates.
\(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal R}\) is a specified norm on \(\mathbb{R}^m\).
Each trust-region model subproblem is solved to prescribed accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure defines a derivative-based residual method adapted to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal R}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual minimization under an explicitly chosen non-Euclidean norm.

notation.meaning: Residual Jacobian at the current iterate.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate, but the statement proposes a specific trust-region framework without evidence and leaves the norm-dependent stationarity measure unspecified. In addition, the plain statement excludes the Euclidean norm while the mathematical statement permits any norm. A source is needed to determine and support the intended other-norm variant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Minimization in a Non-Euclidean Norm
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular, and let \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathsf R}\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional residual minimization using a norm other than the Euclidean norm; smoothness is not assumed for the norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An other-norm residual problem is \[\min_{x\in\mathcal D}\;F_{\mathsf R}(x)=\|D^{-1}R(x)\|_{\mathsf R},\] where \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathsf R}\) is not a positive multiple of \(\|\cdot\|_2\). An other-norm residual method constructs its steps from this objective or an equivalent epigraph formulation and uses subgradients, linear programs, convex programs, or smooth approximations appropriate to the selected norm. The norm, scaling, constraint set, and exact or smoothed interpretation must be fixed as part of the problem specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Other-norm residual methods minimize the size of a scaled residual vector in a specified norm that is not Euclidean. Their models and optimality objects must match that norm; ordinary least-squares normal equations do not define the family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\mathsf R}(x)=\|D^{-1}R(x)\|_{\mathsf R}\) with \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathsf R}\not\equiv c\|\cdot\|_2\) for every \(c>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For any norm, \(\|z\|_{\mathsf R}=\max_{\|u\|_{\mathsf R,*}\leq1}u^Tz\), where \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathsf R,*}\) is the dual norm.
special_cases_latex: For \(\|z\|_1=\sum_i|z_i|\), the problem is least-absolute-residual fitting.
For \(\|z\|_\infty=\max_i|z_i|\), the problem is minimax residual fitting.
immediate_consequences_latex: The \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_\infty\) objectives are generally nonsmooth even when \(R\) is smooth.
boundary_notes: A componentwise robust loss need not be a norm because it may fail positive homogeneity or the triangle inequality.
Squaring a norm preserves minimizers but changes its first-order representation at zero and its model scaling.

notation.meaning: Dual norm of the selected residual norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Derivative-Free Nonlinear Least-Squares Method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be available through residual evaluations and define \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|R(x)\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional nonlinear least squares in which analytic or automatic residual derivatives are not used by the iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative-free nonlinear least-squares method generates trial points using values \(\{R(y):y\in Y_k\}\) at a finite sample set \(Y_k\), without evaluating \(J(y)\) or derivatives of \(f\). It may construct residual models \(m_{i,k}(p)\) satisfying interpolation or regression conditions at sampled displacements and then use the structured objective model \[q_k(p)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m m_{i,k}(p)^2,\] or it may construct a scalar model of \(f\) directly. Acceptance, sample-set maintenance, and radius control are based solely on evaluated residuals and declared model-quality tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative-free nonlinear least-squares method uses sampled residual values, not evaluated derivatives, to choose steps. A structure-exploiting version models each residual and minimizes the sum of squares of those models; a scalar-model version models the least-squares objective directly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Trial steps depend on sampled values \(R(Y_k)\) and not on evaluated \(J\), with a structured model optionally given by \(q_k(p)=\tfrac12\sum_i m_{i,k}(p)^2\).
special_cases_latex: Finite-difference least squares is derivative-free with respect to the user interface but forms a derivative approximation and is treated as a distinct subfamily.
Residual-interpolation methods are structure-exploiting derivative-free least-squares methods.
immediate_consequences_latex: If each residual model is affine, \(q_k\) is a quadratic sum-of-squares model.
boundary_notes: A method is not derivative-free if it obtains exact Jacobian-vector products from automatic differentiation.
The inspected derivative-free source treats general scalar objectives, not this residual-structured family exactly.

notation.meaning: Finite set of sampled points used at iteration k.
Derivative-free local model of the ith residual component.

review_flags: An authoritative source specifically defining derivative-free nonlinear least squares through residual models is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Free Nonlinear Least-Squares Method
Residual-Interpolation Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interpolate each residual from sampled values, minimize the induced least-squares trust-region model, and update both the radius and sample geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given sampled points \(Y_k\) near \(x_k\), construct for every component \(i\) an interpolation model \(m_{i,k}\) satisfying \(m_{i,k}(y)=r_i(y)\) for designated \(y\in Y_k\). Define \(M_k(s)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m m_{i,k}(x_k+s)^2\), compute an approximate minimizer \(s_k\) subject to \(\lVert s\rVert_2\le\Delta_k\), and evaluate \(r(x_k+s_k)\). Accept the trial point and update \(\Delta_k\) according to the ratio of actual to predicted least-squares reduction. Update \(Y_k\) to maintain poised interpolation geometry. Stop when the radius and model-gradient tests meet their tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Residual values are available but derivatives need not be available.
The interpolation set is poised for the selected component-model class.
Trial residual evaluations can be obtained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration defines a residual-interpolation derivative-free nonlinear least-squares method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free least squares using separate interpolation models of residual components.

notation.meaning: Interpolation model of residual component i.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise residual-interpolation algorithm matches the terminal container, but no source supports the selected poisedness, acceptance, geometry-update, and stopping requirements. These details vary among derivative-free nonlinear least-squares methods and require authoritative evidence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Interpolation Least-Squares Model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(Y_k=\{y^0,\ldots,y^s\}\) be sampled points. Let \(\Pi_d^n\) denote scalar polynomials in \(n\) variables of degree at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic derivative-free nonlinear least squares using componentwise polynomial interpolation; regression and underdetermined minimum-change variants require separately declared fitting conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A residual-interpolation model selects \(m_{i,k}\in\Pi_d^n\) for each \(i=1,\ldots,m\) such that \[m_{i,k}(y^j-x_k)=r_i(y^j),\qquad j=0,\ldots,s,\] and forms the structured least-squares model \[q_k(p)=\tfrac12\|m_k(p)\|_2^2=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m m_{i,k}(p)^2.\] A residual-interpolation method computes a step by approximately minimizing \(q_k\) over a declared region, evaluates \(R(x_k+p_k)\), and updates both the sample set and model region according to interpolation-geometry and agreement tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method interpolates every residual component at a common set of sampled points, squares and sums the component models, and chooses a step from that structured model inside a controlled region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_{i,k}(y^j-x_k)=r_i(y^j)\) for all sampled points, and \(q_k(p)=\tfrac12\sum_i m_{i,k}(p)^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For affine residual models \(m_k(p)=c_k+G_kp\), the objective model has Gauss–Newton form \(q_k(p)=\tfrac12\|c_k+G_kp\|_2^2\).
special_cases_latex: With \(d=1\) and \(n+1\) affinely independent sample points, each residual has a unique affine interpolant.
immediate_consequences_latex: A single residual evaluation at a sample point supplies interpolation data for all \(m\) component models.
boundary_notes: Interpolation geometry must be adequate; the equations need not determine unique models for arbitrary sample sets.
Scalar objective interpolation is not residual interpolation because it need not preserve sum-of-squares structure.
The inspected general derivative-free source does not state componentwise residual interpolation.

notation.meaning: Polynomials of total degree at most d in n variables.

review_flags: The available model-based derivative-free locator supports scalar interpolation models only.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Interpolation Least-Squares Model
Finite-Difference Least-Squares Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate the residual Jacobian by finite differences, solve the resulting least-squares model, globalize the step, and adapt differencing increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\tfrac12\lVert r(x)\rVert_2^2\), choose nonzero increments \(h_{k,j}\) and form \((\widehat J_k)_{:,j}=[r(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-r(x_k)]/h_{k,j}\). Compute \(s_k\) from a regularized or trust-region least-squares model, for example by minimizing \(\tfrac12\lVert r(x_k)+\widehat J_ks\rVert_2^2+\tfrac{\mu_k}{2}\lVert s\rVert_2^2\). Accept or damp the step using actual reduction in \(F\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ks_k\), and adapt the increments to truncation and evaluation error. Stop when a finite-difference first-order measure is below tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is continuously differentiable near the iterates.
All required perturbed residual evaluations are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure is a finite-difference nonlinear least-squares method with approximate Jacobian \(\widehat J_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear least squares with a finite-difference approximation to the residual Jacobian.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and finite-difference least-squares idea fit the container, but the cited sources separately cover finite-difference Newton methods and generic least squares; they do not clearly support this specialized combined algorithm. The statement also uses alpha_k and e_j without explicitly defining their domains or roles and gives no precise increment adaptation rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Difference Nonlinear Least Squares
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|R(x)\|_2^2\), and let \(e_j\) be the jth coordinate vector. Assume the required perturbed points lie in \(\mathcal D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic residuals evaluated in finite precision; forward and central componentwise Jacobian approximations are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite-difference least-squares method replaces the analytic residual Jacobian by a matrix \(A_k\) whose columns are obtained from residual evaluations. The forward formula is \[(A_k)_{:j}=\frac{R(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-R(x_k)}{h_{k,j}},\qquad h_{k,j}\ne0,\] and the central formula is \[(A_k)_{:j}=\frac{R(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-R(x_k-h_{k,j}e_j)}{2h_{k,j}}.\] It then forms a least-squares step from \(R(x_k)+A_kp\), such as \(\min_p\tfrac12\|R(x_k)+A_kp\|_2^2\), with optional damping, bounds, or a trust region. Step sizes may vary by coordinate and must account for scaling and evaluation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method estimates every Jacobian column by perturbing a variable and differencing residual vectors, then uses the approximate Jacobian in a Gauss–Newton, damped, or trust-region least-squares model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A_k)_{:j}=[R(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-R(x_k)]/h_{k,j}\) for forward differences, followed by a step based on \(R(x_k)+A_kp\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The forward approximation uses \(n\) additional residual-vector evaluations when columns are differenced separately.
Central differencing uses two perturbed residual-vector evaluations per coordinate and has higher truncation order for sufficiently smooth residuals.
special_cases_latex: Known Jacobian sparsity may permit simultaneous noninterfering coordinate perturbations.
immediate_consequences_latex: With exact arithmetic and differentiable \(R\), each forward-difference column converges to the corresponding Jacobian column as \(h_{k,j}\to0\).
boundary_notes: Arbitrarily small differences can amplify roundoff or residual-evaluation noise.
Secant updates reusing inter-iterate differences are not identical to fresh coordinate finite differences.

notation.meaning: Finite-difference approximation to the residual Jacobian at x_k.
Nonzero difference interval for coordinate j.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Aware Residual-Model Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build residual models only at resolvable scales, compare reductions against noise uncertainty, and report when further progress is noise-limited.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose evaluations satisfy \(\widetilde r(x)=r(x)+\varepsilon(x)\) with a known or estimated bound \(\lVert\varepsilon(x)\rVert_2\le\eta(x)\). At \(x_k\), fit residual models from samples whose radii exceed the noise-resolution scale. Compute a trust-region step from the induced least-squares model, but accept it only when predicted and observed reductions exceed prescribed multiples of the corresponding uncertainty bounds. If reduction is unresolved, enlarge sampling increments, resample, or terminate with a noise-limited flag rather than shrinking indefinitely. Output an accepted iterate together with the final stationarity and noise-resolution thresholds.
assumptions_latex: Observed residuals obey the stated deterministic error bound.
The residual model is fitted from a geometrically adequate sample set.
Acceptance thresholds account for uncertainty in both compared evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure prevents model acceptance and radius refinement from relying on reductions indistinguishable from noise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free residual modeling with explicit safeguards against evaluation noise.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the noise-aware residual-model container, but the proposed resolution scale, uncertainty-aware acceptance test, resampling behavior, and noise-limited termination are method-dependent and currently unsupported. An authoritative source is required to make these rules mathematically definite.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noise-Aware Residual Model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Suppose evaluations return \(\widetilde R(x)=R(x)+\varepsilon(x)\in\mathbb R^m\), with a declared componentwise or normwise bound \(\|\varepsilon(x)\|\leq\delta(x)\). Let \(m_k(p)\) be a local model built from noisy samples.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic bounded evaluation error in residual values; stochastic-noise methods require probabilistic accuracy conditions instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A noise-aware residual-model method is a residual-based iteration whose model construction and acceptance tests explicitly use an error scale \(\delta\). Its interpolation or regression conditions are relaxed to consistency conditions such as \[\|m_k(y-x_k)-\widetilde R(y)\|\leq c\,\delta(y),\qquad y\in Y_k,\] and a trial step is accepted as producing resolved decrease only when the observed change in the merit function exceeds a declared multiple of the uncertainty induced by the noisy residual evaluations. Model radii, difference intervals, and termination tolerances are not reduced below declared noise-dependent floors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noise-aware residual-model method represents residual evaluations as true values plus bounded error, fits models only to the accuracy justified by that error, and refuses to interpret changes smaller than the induced uncertainty as reliable progress.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model fitting satisfies a noise-scaled consistency condition and step acceptance requires observed reduction larger than a declared uncertainty threshold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A weighted condition may use \(\|D_\delta(y)^{-1}(m_k(y-x_k)-\widetilde R(y))\|\leq c\) when componentwise error bounds are available.
special_cases_latex: When \(\delta\equiv0\), exact interpolation and ordinary deterministic model tests are recovered.
immediate_consequences_latex: A termination tolerance below the residual-evaluation uncertainty is not certified by this model.
Finite-difference intervals must balance truncation error against amplified evaluation noise.
boundary_notes: Unknown or adversarial error without a bound cannot support the deterministic consistency test stated here.
The available sources discuss noise in finite differences and scalar derivative-free models, but not this precise residual-model family.

notation.meaning: Declared bound on residual-evaluation error at x.

review_flags: A source specifically supporting residual-vector model consistency and acceptance thresholds under bounded noise is needed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear Equation Method Family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\). A root is \(x_*\in\mathcal D\) satisfying \(F(x_*)=0\). When \(F\) is differentiable, write \(J(x)=F'(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square finite-dimensional nonlinear systems; rectangular systems and least-squares stationarity are outside the canonical root-finding form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear equation method is an iteration \[x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\] whose defining local equation, fixed-point map, secant condition, continuation equation, or residual model is constructed with the primary destination \(F(x)=0\). The nonlinear equation method families include exact or inexact Newton methods based on \(F(x_k)+J(x_k)s\), secant or quasi-Newton methods replacing \(J(x_k)\), fixed-point iterations \(x_{k+1}=G(x_k)\) with \(F(x)=0\iff G(x)=x\), higher-order residual models, and continuation methods tracking solutions of \(H(x,t)=0\) toward \(H(x,1)=F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear equation methods seek an actual root of a square residual map. Their step equations or maps are built to make the residual zero, unlike generic minimization of a residual norm, which may stop at a nonzero stationary point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution set targeted by the family is \(F^{-1}(0)=\{x\in\mathcal D:F(x)=0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D\) satisfies \(F(x)=0\iff G(x)=x\), root finding is equivalently fixed-point computation.
special_cases_latex: For \(F=\nabla f\), a nonlinear equation method targets stationary points of \(f\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every root globally minimizes \(\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\) with value zero, but a stationary point of that merit function need not be a root.
boundary_notes: The definition does not guarantee existence, uniqueness, or convergence to a root.
Methods whose sole stated destination is an arbitrary stationary point of \(\tfrac12\|F\|^2\) are not placed in this family.

notation.meaning: Set of roots of the nonlinear system.
Parameterized residual used by a continuation method.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact interpolatory tensor model and safeguarded step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An algorithmic representation for square nonlinear residual systems; it does not assert a convergence rate or guarantee for degenerate roots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) have Jacobian \(J\), let \(q\ge 1\), and set \(s_{jk}=x_{k-j}-x_k\). Define
\[
\widehat M_k(p)=r(x_k)+J(x_k)p+\tfrac12T_kpp,
\qquad
T_kuv=\sum_{\ell=1}^q a_\ell(s_{\ell k}^Tu)(s_{\ell k}^Tv).
\]
If the vectors \(a_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^n\) are chosen so that
\[
\tfrac12T_ks_{jk}s_{jk}=r(x_{k-j})-r(x_k)-J(x_k)s_{jk},
\qquad j=1,\ldots,q,
\]
then
\[
\widehat M_k(s_{jk})=r(x_{k-j}),\qquad j=1,\ldots,q.
\]
The representation stores the \(2q\) vectors \(\{a_\ell,s_{\ell k}\}_{\ell=1}^q\), requiring \(2nq\) scalar locations. If \(\widehat M_k(p)=0\) has no solution, the method may instead choose a minimizer of \(\|\widehat M_k(p)\|_2^2\). If this step is not a descent direction for \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2\), it may be replaced, when \(J(x_k)\) is nonsingular, by \(-J(x_k)^{-1}r(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a square nonlinear residual system, the tensor method augments the Newton model with a quadratic tensor term. A compact representation based on previous displacements can be selected to interpolate residual values at retained iterates and uses 2nq scalar storage locations. The tensor-model equation need not have a root; in that case the method may minimize the squared model residual. A resulting non-descent step may be replaced by the Newton step when the Jacobian is nonsingular.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region algorithm for nonlinear equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance and radius-update framework using a linearized residual trust-region subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given $\bar\Delta>0$, $\Delta_0\in(0,\bar\Delta)$, and $\eta\in[0,\tfrac14)$, for $k=0,1,\ldots$ compute an approximate solution $p_k$ of
\[
\min_{\|p\|\leq\Delta_k}\tfrac12\|r_k+J_kp\|_2^2
\]
and evaluate
\[
\rho_k=\frac{\|r_k\|^2-\|r(x_k+p_k)\|^2}{\|r_k\|^2-\|r_k+J_kp_k\|^2}.
\]
Set
\[
\Delta_{k+1}=\begin{cases}
\tfrac14\|p_k\|,&\rho_k<\tfrac14,\\
\min\{2\Delta_k,\bar\Delta\},&\rho_k>\tfrac34\text{ and }\|p_k\|=\Delta_k,\\
\Delta_k,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+p_k,&\rho_k>\eta,\\x_k,&\rho_k\leq\eta.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize the linearized residual model within the current trust region. Shrink the radius when agreement is below one quarter, double it up to the prescribed maximum when agreement exceeds three quarters and the step reaches the boundary, and otherwise retain it. Accept the step exactly when the agreement ratio is strictly greater than eta.
assumptions_latex: p_k\text{ approximately solves the stated residual trust-region subproblem}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_{k+1},\Delta_{k+1})\text{ is determined by the displayed acceptance and radius-update rules for every }k\geq0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularized residual trust-region steps and sufficient inexact-step safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual trust-region step representation, Levenberg–Marquardt interpretation, inexact-step requirements, and an LP-representable alternative residual model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_{\|p\|\leq\Delta_k}\tfrac12\|r_k+J_kp\|_2^2,
\]
an exact solution admits the representation
\[
p_k=-(J_k^TJ_k+\lambda_kI)^{-1}J_k^Tr_k
\]
for some $\lambda_k\geq0$ whenever the displayed inverse exists. If the unconstrained step $p_k^{\mathrm J}$ exists and satisfies $\|p_k^{\mathrm J}\|\leq\Delta_k$, then $\lambda_k=0$. This is the residual trust-region form associated with Levenberg--Marquardt regularization.

Exact recovery of the trust-region parameter is unnecessary for the cited global-convergence framework when the computed regularized steps satisfy, for iteration-independent constants $c_1>0$ and $\gamma\geq1$,
\[
m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\geq c_1\|J_k^Tr_k\|\min\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\|J_k^Tr_k\|}{\|J_k^TJ_k\|}\right\},
\qquad \|p_k\|\leq\gamma\Delta_k.
\]
An alternative residual model using an $\ell_1$ merit function and an $\ell_\infty$ trust region is
\[
\min_p\|J_kp+r_k\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|p\|_\infty\leq\Delta,
\]
and this subproblem is representable as a linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact Euclidean residual trust-region step has a Levenberg–Marquardt regularized Gauss–Newton form with a nonnegative parameter, which is zero when the unconstrained step exists and is feasible. Exact parameter recovery is unnecessary for the cited global-convergence framework if the computed steps uniformly achieve Cauchy-type decrease and obey the stated enlarged-radius bound. With an l1 residual objective and an l-infinity trust region, the residual subproblem can instead be formulated as a linear program.
assumptions_latex: J_k^TJ_k+\lambda_kI\text{ is invertible whenever the displayed inverse representation is used}
p_k^{\mathrm J}\text{ exists for the stated feasible-unconstrained-step implication}
c_1>0\text{ and }\gamma\geq1\text{ are independent of }k\text{ for the inexact-step guarantee}
p_k\text{ is generated and accepted within the stated residual trust-region framework}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k=-(J_k^TJ_k+\lambda_kI)^{-1}J_k^Tr_k,\ \lambda_k\geq0;\quad \|p_k^{\mathrm J}\|\leq\Delta_k\Rightarrow\lambda_k=0;\quad \text{the displayed decrease and norm conditions are sufficient step hypotheses for the cited global-convergence results; and the }\ell_1/\ell_\infty\text{ subproblem is LP-representable}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit tangent characterization of an arclength-parameterized zero path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies at a regular point of a continuously differentiable homotopy zero path; orientation by comparison with the preceding tangent is a practical sign-selection heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H be continuously differentiable near a path (x(s),\lambda(s)) satisfying H(x(s),\lambda(s))=0 and (x(0),\lambda(0))=(a,0), with s denoting arc length. Then H_x(x,\lambda)\dot{x}+H_\lambda(x,\lambda)\dot{\lambda}=0 and \|\dot{x}\|_2^2+|\dot{\lambda}|^2=1. If [H_x\;H_\lambda]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n+1)} has full row rank n, its null space is one-dimensional, so the unit tangent is determined up to sign. A consistent orientation may be selected by requiring an acute angle with the preceding tangent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiating the zero-path equation places the path tangent in the null space of the augmented homotopy derivative. At a full-row-rank point that null space is one-dimensional; unit normalization gives an arclength tangent up to sign, and comparison with the preceding tangent supplies a practical orientation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Homotopy tangent calculation by column-pivoted QR factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Requires full row rank so that the triangular factor is nonsingular; sign continuity additionally requires a preceding oriented tangent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A=[H_x(x,\lambda)\;H_\lambda(x,\lambda)]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n+1)} have rank n. Compute Q^TA\Pi=[R\;w], where Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} is orthogonal, R\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} is nonsingular upper triangular, \Pi\in\mathbb{R}^{(n+1)\times(n+1)} is a permutation matrix, and w\in\mathbb{R}^n. Set v=\Pi\begin{bmatrix}R^{-1}w\\-1\end{bmatrix}. Then Av=0. Set (\dot{x},\dot{\lambda})=\pm v/\|v\|_2, choosing the sign to make an acute angle with the preceding tangent when orientation continuity is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column-pivoted QR reduces the augmented homotopy derivative to a triangular system and yields an explicit null vector. Normalizing that vector gives the unit path tangent, whose sign can be selected consistently with the previous tangent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary-variable reformulations of one- and infinity-norm residual minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise epigraph representations and their consequence for optimization over a smooth residual map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r:X\to\mathbb{R}^m. For every x\in X,\qquad \|r(x)\|_1=\min_{t\in\mathbb{R}^m}\left\{\mathbf{1}^\top t:-t_i\le r_i(x)\le t_i\ \text{for all }i\right\},\qquad \|r(x)\|_\infty=\min_{\tau\in\mathbb{R}}\left\{\tau:-\tau\le r_i(x)\le\tau\ \text{for all }i\right\}.\qquad Consequently, minimizing either residual norm over x is equivalent to minimizing the corresponding linear auxiliary objective subject to these inequalities; if every r_i is smooth, the resulting formulation is a smooth constrained optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a vector residual r(x), its one-norm equals the minimum sum of componentwise upper bounds on the absolute residuals, and its infinity norm equals the minimum common upper bound on all absolute residuals. Thus minimizing either norm is equivalent to a constrained problem with a linear auxiliary objective. When the residual components are smooth, this is a smooth constrained optimization formulation.
assumptions_latex: r_i\text{ is smooth for every }i\text{ when claiming a smooth constrained formulation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|r(x)\|_1=\min_t\{\mathbf{1}^\top t:-t_i\le r_i(x)\le t_i\ \forall i\},\quad \|r(x)\|_\infty=\min_\tau\{\tau:-\tau\le r_i(x)\le\tau\ \forall i\},\quad\text{and the corresponding minimization problems admit equivalent smooth constrained formulations when }r\text{ is smooth}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Square nonlinear systems and roots
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the problem class and records its residual-squares representation and possible absence or multiplicity of roots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n, with r(x)=(r_1(x),\ldots,r_n(x))^T, and suppose each r_i is smooth. The square nonlinear-equation problem is to find x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n such that r(x^*)=0; such an x^* is called a solution or root. Moreover, r(x^*)=0 if and only if \sum_{i=1}^n r_i(x^*)^2=0. The solution set may be empty, a singleton, or contain multiple points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth vector function from R^n to R^n, solving the square nonlinear system means finding a point where every residual is zero; that point is a solution or root. This is equivalent to attaining zero in the residual sum of squares. A system can have no root, one root, or multiple roots.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ is a root}\iff r(x^*)=0\iff \sum_{i=1}^n r_i(x^*)^2=0,\qquad \{x:r(x)=0\}\text{ may be empty, singleton, or non-singleton.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Method for a Square Nonlinear System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable, let \(J(x)=F'(x)\), and choose \(x_0\in\mathcal D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure finite-dimensional Newton iteration for square systems; damping, trust regions, inexact linear solves, and singular-Jacobian variants are neighboring extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every iteration \(k\) for which the linear system is solvable and the new point remains in \(\mathcal D\), the Newton step \(s_k\) is defined by \[J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k.\] Equivalently, \(s_k\) is a zero of the affine residual model \(M_k(s)=F(x_k)+J(x_k)s\). If \(J(x_k)\) is nonsingular, the step is uniquely \(s_k=-J(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton's method linearizes the nonlinear residual at the current iterate, chooses the step that makes this affine model zero, and adds that step to the current point. A nonsingular current Jacobian makes the step unique.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(J(x_k)\) is invertible, \(x_{k+1}=x_k-J(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(F=\nabla f\), the iteration is the pure Newton method for unconstrained stationary equations.
If \(F\) is affine with nonsingular Jacobian, one Newton step reaches its unique root.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(F(x_k)=0\), then \(s_k=0\) is a Newton step.
A singular Jacobian can make the pure Newton step nonexistent or nonunique.
boundary_notes: This definition makes no global-convergence assertion from a remote initial point.
Solving \(J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)\) only approximately defines an inexact Newton method, not the pure method in this slot.
Least-squares solutions of inconsistent Newton equations require a separately specified rectangular or singular-system variant.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the exact Jacobian linearization of a square nonlinear system at each iterate and update toward a root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), an initial point \(x_0\), and tolerance \(\tau>0\), evaluate the exact Jacobian \(J_F(x_k)\) and solve \(J_F(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\); a globalized variant may replace the full step by an accepted damped or trust-region step without changing the exact-Jacobian Newton model. Terminate successfully when \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\le\tau\), and report failure if the linear system is unsolvable or the globalization mechanism cannot accept a step. The output is the final iterate and its residual norm.

The exact Jacobian can be evaluated.
The Newton linear system is nonsingular whenever a full Newton step is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Newton iteration for a square nonlinear system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(F:D\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, and write \(J(x)=F'(x)\). The problem is to find \(x_*\in D\) satisfying \(F(x_*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, deterministic root finding. “Exact” means that the current analytic Jacobian is used and the Newton linear equation is solved exactly; it does not assert exact arithmetic or global convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact Newton root method is the iteration defined, whenever \(J(x_k)\) is nonsingular and \(x_k+s_k\in D\), by \[J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k.\] Equivalently, \(x_{k+1}\) is the zero of the current affine model \(M_k(x_k+p)=F(x_k)+J(x_k)p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously differentiable square residual map, exact Newton forms the affine model at the current iterate, solves the current Jacobian equation \(J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)\) without a linear-solve residual, and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). The iteration is defined only when the required linear equation is solvable and the new point remains in the domain.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[x_{k+1}=x_k-J(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\quad\text{when }J(x_k)^{-1}\text{ exists}.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(n=1\), the update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k-F(x_k)/F'(x_k)\).
If \(F(x)=Ax-b\) with nonsingular \(A\), one Newton update produces the root from every starting point.
immediate_consequences_latex: The Newton step is uniquely determined whenever \(J(x_k)\) is nonsingular.
The defining linear residual \(J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\) is zero.
boundary_notes: A damped update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ks_k\) with \(\alpha_k\ne1\) is a globalization variant, not the pure iteration defined here.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Connections and failure boundaries of exact Newton root iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method connections, singular-Jacobian failure, remote-start behavior, and a degenerate-root rate counterexample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the iteration $J(x_k)p_k=-r(x_k)$, $x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k$, choosing $r=\nabla f$ recovers Newton's method for unconstrained optimization, and applying the iteration to the first-order optimality equations of an equality-constrained problem gives the associated sequential quadratic programming construction. In the usual case where $J(x_k)$ is nonsingular, the displayed Newton equation is also equivalent to the cited Gauss--Newton equation. A remote starting point may lead to erratic behavior, and if $J(x_k)$ is singular the Newton step may fail to be defined. For the degenerate scalar residual $r(x)=x^2$ with $x_0\ne0$, $$x_{k+1}=\frac12x_k,\qquad x_k=2^{-k}x_0,$$ so the iterates converge to $0$ only Q-linearly. Jacobian Lipschitz continuity on a domain means that some $\beta_L\ge0$ satisfies $$\|J(x)-J(y)\|\le\beta_L\|x-y\|$$ for all $x,y$ in that domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root-finding Newton recovers optimization Newton when the residual is a gradient and produces the equality-constrained SQP construction when applied to the first-order optimality system. Under the stated nonsingularity qualification it also agrees with the cited Gauss–Newton equation. Remote starts may behave erratically, and a singular Jacobian may leave the Newton step undefined. For the degenerate residual r(x)=x², every nonzero starting value is halved at each iteration, giving only linear convergence to zero. The paragraph also defines Lipschitz continuity of the Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: J(x_k)\text{ is nonsingular for the stated Gauss--Newton equivalence}
r(x)=x^2,\quad x_0\ne0\text{ for the degenerate-root example}
\exists\beta_L\ge0\ \forall x,y\text{ in the domain}:\ \|J(x)-J(y)\|\le\beta_L\|x-y\|\text{ for Jacobian Lipschitz continuity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r=\nabla f\Rightarrow\text{unconstrained-optimization Newton};\quad r(x)=x^2\Rightarrow x_k=2^{-k}x_0\text{ with Q-linear convergence};\quad J(x_k)\text{ singular permits failure of step definition}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton iterations with a reused Jacobian
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable with Jacobian \(J\), and let \(\tau:\mathbb{N}_0\to\mathbb{N}_0\) satisfy \(0\leq\tau(k)\leq k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth root finding with exact derivative evaluations performed only at selected refresh iterations. The definition covers chord and block-reuse variants but excludes secant updates that alter the stored matrix without reevaluating the derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative-reuse Newton method selects refresh indices through \(\tau(k)\), forms \(B_k=J(x_{\tau(k)})\), and, whenever \(B_k\) is nonsingular, defines \[B_ks_k=-F(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k.\] Reuse occurs at iteration \(k\) precisely when \(\tau(k)<k\), equivalently \(B_k=B_{k-1}\) without a new Jacobian evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative-reuse Newton method solves the Newton-like equation with an exact Jacobian evaluated at an earlier retained iterate. A refresh map \(\tau(k)\) chooses the stored matrix \(B_k=J(x_{\tau(k)})\); the method solves \(B_ks_k=-F(x_k)\) and accepts \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). At reuse iterations no new derivative matrix is formed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: On a refresh block \(k=r,\ldots,r+q-1\), \[J(x_r)s_k=-F(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k.\]
special_cases_latex: Pure Newton is recovered by \(\tau(k)=k\).
The chord method is recovered by \(\tau(k)=0\) for every \(k\).
Periodic refresh with period \(q\) uses \(\tau(k)=q\lfloor k/q\rfloor\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every reuse block requires only one Jacobian formation and factorization, although it may require several triangular solves.
The equation residual relative to the stored matrix is zero, while \(J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\) need not vanish.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a refresh test or claim a convergence rate.
If \(B_k\) is updated by secant data rather than set equal to a previously evaluated Jacobian, the method is quasi-Newton rather than derivative-reuse Newton.

notation.meaning: index of the iterate whose Jacobian is retained at iteration k

review_flags: No inspected source in the supplied locator set gave a precise canonical definition of chord, periodic-refresh, and general refresh-map variants in this root-equation scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton iterations with a reused Jacobian
Modified Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the current exact Jacobian by a nonsingular modified approximation, solve the resulting Newton equation, and refresh that approximation according to a rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), choose an initial point \(x_0\) and construct nonsingular matrices \(B_k\) that approximate \(J_F(x_k)\), possibly by retaining selected derivative information across iterations. Solve \(B_ks_k=-F(x_k)\), select \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) through the prescribed globalization rule, and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ks_k\). Refresh or modify \(B_k\) whenever its update criterion is triggered. Stop when \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\) or an accepted correction norm is below tolerance; output the iterate, residual norm, and final approximation \(B_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable near the iterates.
Every matrix \(B_k\) used in a step is nonsingular.
The globalization and matrix-refresh rules are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed scheme is a modified Newton family, reducing to exact Newton when \(B_k=J_F(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton root iteration using a deliberately modified or reused Jacobian matrix.

notation.meaning: Modified Jacobian approximation used at iteration k.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is suitable, but the formulation permits arbitrary Jacobian approximations and therefore extends beyond the derivative-reuse branch into quasi-Newton and other inexact-Newton families. A source is required to determine the intended meaning of modified Newton in this exact container and to delimit the admissible matrix modifications or reuse rules.

knowledge_statements.title: Chord Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix one Jacobian approximation, reuse its factorization for every Newton-like correction, and iterate until the nonlinear residual is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(x_0\), form the fixed matrix \(B=J_F(x_0)\), or another prescribed nonsingular approximation constructed once. For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), solve \(Bs_k=-F(x_k)\) and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ks_k\), where \(\alpha_k=1\) for the classical local chord method and may be reduced by a stated globalization test. Reuse the same factorization of \(B\) at every iteration. Stop when the residual or correction meets tolerance, and report breakdown if the fixed linear system cannot be solved or no step is accepted.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable near the iterates.
Residual evaluations remain available throughout the iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kB^{-1}F(x_k)\) defines the chord method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton-like root iteration with one Jacobian matrix fixed across all corrections.

notation.meaning: Single fixed Jacobian or Jacobian approximation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-matrix iteration correctly captures the core chord-method idea and the algorithm kind fits the container. An authoritative source is nevertheless required, particularly for the broadened version allowing a matrix other than J_F(x_0) and an added globalization mechanism.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Refresh Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A refresh regime is an explicit predicate deciding whether to recompute the Jacobian or retain the matrix used in the preceding correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k\) be the derivative matrix used to compute \(s_k\) from \(B_ks_k=-F(x_k)\). A derivative-refresh regime is a predicate \(R_k\in\{0,1\}\) determined from available iteration data, together with the update rule \(B_{k+1}=J_F(x_{k+1})\) when \(R_k=1\) and \(B_{k+1}=B_k\) when \(R_k=0\). Admissible examples include periodic refresh, refresh after rejected or insufficiently decreasing steps, and refresh when a discrepancy such as \(\lVert F(x_{k+1})-F(x_k)-B_ks_k\rVert\) exceeds a specified threshold. The regime must also declare mandatory refresh after singularity or linear-solve breakdown.
assumptions_latex: The iteration data required by \(R_k\) are observable.
An exact or designated replacement derivative can be computed when refresh is requested.
All thresholds and mandatory-refresh events are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((R_k,B_{k+1})\) completely determines derivative reuse versus refresh after iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rules specifying when a reused derivative model must be recomputed.

notation.meaning: Derivative matrix currently used by the root solver.
Correction computed with the current derivative matrix.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind appropriately describes a refresh rule rather than a complete solver. However, the proposed predicate formalization, discrepancy trigger, and mandatory refresh events are method-dependent and unsupported, so a source is needed to establish the intended derivative-refresh regime taxonomy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton root methods using a freshly approximated Jacobian
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and suppose function values are available while the exact Jacobian is unavailable or deliberately not used. Let \(A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be constructed at \(x_k\) as an approximation to \(J(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional root finding with a derivative approximation freshly constructed at each designated iteration. This includes finite-difference and other direct derivative approximations, but not secant matrices propagated solely from earlier steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative-approximation Newton method is an iteration \[A_ks_k=-F(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k,\] where \(A_k\) is computed as an approximation to \(J(x_k)\) without evaluating the exact Jacobian. In the forward-difference instance, for nonzero increments \(h_{k,j}\), \[A_ke_j=\frac{F(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-F(x_k)}{h_{k,j}},\qquad j=1,\ldots,n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, this family constructs a matrix \(A_k\) intended to approximate the current Jacobian without evaluating the exact derivative, solves \(A_ks_k=-F(x_k)\), and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). A canonical instance builds each column by a forward difference of residual values along a coordinate direction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The step is the zero of the approximate affine model \(\widetilde M_k(x_k+p)=F(x_k)+A_kp\).
special_cases_latex: Forward differences use \(A_ke_j=[F(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-F(x_k)]/h_{k,j}\).
Central differences may use \(A_ke_j=[F(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-F(x_k-h_{k,j}e_j)]/(2h_{k,j})\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Even when the equation with \(A_k\) is solved exactly, the true Newton residual \(J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\) generally is nonzero.
A dense coordinate forward-difference Jacobian requires \(n\) perturbed residual evaluations in addition to an available value \(F(x_k)\).
boundary_notes: The finite-difference increment must be nonzero and keep every sampled point inside \(D\).
Jacobian-free products used only inside an iterative Krylov solve belong to the Jacobian-free Newton–Krylov family.
Matrices updated from secant pairs rather than reconstructed at the current point belong to quasi-Newton methods.

notation.meaning: fresh approximation to the current Jacobian
