knowledge_statements.statement_title: Type-I and Type-II Anderson multisecant duality
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(r(x)=G(x)-x\), define \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\), \(y_i=r(x_{i+1})-r(x_i)\), and retained matrices \(S_k=[s_i]_{i\in I_k}\), \(Y_k=[y_i]_{i\in I_k}\). Let \(B_0\) and \(H_0\) be reference direct and inverse residual-Jacobian models.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic direct-versus-inverse multisecant formulations of Anderson-type updates; no unconditional equality of the resulting matrices is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Type-I/Type-II dual description associates Type I with a direct model \(B_k\) satisfying \(B_kS_k=Y_k\) and Type II with an inverse model \(H_k\) satisfying \(H_kY_k=S_k\). Each model is selected from its affine multisecant set by a specified least-change or regularized criterion relative to \(B_0\) or \(H_0\). Their steps are defined by \(B_kp_k=-r(x_k)\) and \(p_k=-H_kr(x_k)\), respectively. The pair is exactly inverse-dual only when both selected matrices are nonsingular and the selection rules enforce \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\); the two multisecant equations alone do not enforce that identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type-I Anderson models the residual Jacobian and satisfies \(B_kS_k=Y_k\); Type II models its inverse and satisfies \(H_kY_k=S_k\). Both require a matrix-selection rule. They are exact algebraic inverses only under additional compatibility and nonsingularity conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\), then \(B_kS_k=Y_k\) and \(H_kY_k=S_k\) are equivalent.
Without inverse compatibility, the two equations define distinct affine spaces of matrix approximations.
special_cases_latex: With a single stored pair, the direct and inverse descriptions reduce to one-secant quasi-Newton models.
With zero history, the reference model determines the step.
immediate_consequences_latex: Whenever \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\), Type-I and Type-II formulas produce the same step for the same residual.
boundary_notes: Using analogous unweighted Frobenius least-change rules does not automatically make the selected matrices inverses.
Rank-deficient history requires pseudoinverse, regularization, deletion, or restart conventions.
review_flags: A precise source is needed for the nomenclature and the exact least-change formulations of Anderson Type I and Type II.
knowledge_statements.title: Type-I and Type-II Anderson multisecant duality
Type-I Anderson Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type-I Anderson acceleration fits a direct residual-Jacobian approximation to recent multisecant data and takes its quasi-Newton step, regularizing dependent history when necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), set \(r(x)=G(x)-x\) and choose memory \(m\), initial point \(x_0\), and nonsingular baseline matrices \(B_k^{(0)}\). At iteration \(k\), form retained differences
\[
S_k=[x_{i+1}-x_i],\qquad Y_k=[r(x_{i+1})-r(x_i)],
\]
using at most the last \(m\) indices. A Type-I variant constructs a direct residual-Jacobian model
\[
B_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B}\lVert B-B_k^{(0)}\rVert_F
\quad\text{subject to}\quad BS_k=Y_k,
\]
possibly after regularizing or dropping dependent columns, and updates \(x_{k+1}=x_k-B_k^{-1}r(x_k)\). Stop at a prescribed residual, step, or iteration threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is evaluable at every generated iterate.
The retained multisecant constraints are feasible after safeguarding.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-Jacobian multisecant form of Anderson acceleration.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate role, but Type-I Anderson conventions vary across authoritative treatments, so the direct-Jacobian formulation and baseline least-change model require a specific source. The bracket notation for S_k and Y_k also fails to state the retained index range explicitly.

knowledge_statements.title: Type-II Anderson Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type-II Anderson chooses the minimum-norm residual-difference least-squares coefficients and corrects a mixed fixed-point step using the corresponding iterate and residual differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), let \(f(x)=g(x)-x\), and let \(m_k\leq m\). Form \(\Delta X_k=[x_{j+1}-x_j]_{j=k-m_k}^{k-1}\) and \(\Delta F_k=[f(x_{j+1})-f(x_j)]_{j=k-m_k}^{k-1}\). Choose \(\gamma_k=\Delta F_k^{\dagger}f(x_k)\), the minimum-norm member of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in\mathbb R^{m_k}}\|f(x_k)-\Delta F_k\gamma\|_2\), and update
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta_k f(x_k)-(\Delta X_k+\beta_k\Delta F_k)\gamma_k,\qquad 0<\beta_k\leq1.\]
When \(m_k=0\), use the convention \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta_kf(x_k)\).
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is evaluable at every generated iterate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard depth-limited Type-II Anderson step with optional scalar mixing.

notation.meaning: stored iterate and residual difference matrices

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Type-II Anderson least-squares formulation

knowledge_statements.title: Type-I versus Type-II Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With full square secant history, Type-I and Type-II models are exact inverses and generate identical steps; this equivalence can fail for incomplete or deficient history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), and suppose the square history matrices \(\Delta X,\Delta F\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) are nonsingular. A Type-I Jacobian model satisfying \(J\Delta X=\Delta F\) is uniquely \(J=\Delta F\Delta X^{-1}\). A Type-II inverse-Jacobian model satisfying \(H\Delta F=\Delta X\) is uniquely \(H=\Delta X\Delta F^{-1}\). Consequently,
\[H=J^{-1},\qquad -H F(x)=-J^{-1}F(x).\]
Thus the Type-I linear solve and the Type-II inverse action produce the same step. With rectangular or rank-deficient histories, least-change or pseudoinverse completions need not be mutual inverses.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta X,\Delta F\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J=\Delta F\Delta X^{-1}\), \(H=\Delta X\Delta F^{-1}=J^{-1}\), and the two steps coincide.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse multisecant correspondence under square, nonsingular history matrices.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary square multisecant inverse correspondence

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The square nonsingular correspondence is algebraically precise and the duality content kind fits the leaf. However, no citation supports its identification with Anderson Type-I/Type-II models or the additional claim about rectangular and rank-deficient completions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safeguarded Anderson update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G:X\to X\), let \(r(x)=G(x)-x\), let \(x_k^{\mathrm{AA}}\) be an Anderson candidate computed from retained history, and let \(x_k^{\mathrm{base}}=G(x_k)\) or another prescribed globally controlled base candidate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance-control wrappers around an Anderson candidate; the particular merit function and thresholds are parameters of the variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An Anderson safeguard-control variant is specified by an acceptance predicate \(\mathcal C_k:X\to\{0,1\}\), constructed from quantities available at iteration \(k\), and the update \(x_{k+1}=x_k^{\mathrm{AA}}\) if \(\mathcal C_k(x_k^{\mathrm{AA}})=1\), while \(x_{k+1}=x_k^{\mathrm{base}}\) otherwise. A residual safeguard is obtained by choosing a nonnegative reference value \(R_k\) and threshold \(\eta_k\geq0\), and accepting only when \(\|r(x_k^{\mathrm{AA}})\|\leq\eta_kR_k\). The definition is complete only after specifying the base candidate, reference sequence, acceptance test, and whether rejection triggers damping, history deletion, or restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguarded Anderson method first computes an accelerated candidate, tests it using an explicit acceptance rule, and otherwise takes a prescribed base step. A common formal test bounds the candidate residual by a threshold times a reference residual value.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The binary rule can be expressed by an indicator \(a_k\in\{0,1\}\): \(x_{k+1}=a_kx_k^{\mathrm{AA}}+(1-a_k)x_k^{\mathrm{base}}\).
special_cases_latex: A monotone residual safeguard takes \(R_k=\|r(x_k)\|\) and \(0\leq\eta_k\leq1\).
A restart safeguard discards the retained history whenever the Anderson candidate is rejected.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every rejected acceleration step is replaced by the explicitly specified base candidate.
boundary_notes: A safeguard definition alone gives no global convergence result unless the base method and acceptance schedule satisfy additional hypotheses.
Tests requiring evaluation of \(r(x_k^{\mathrm{AA}})\) incur an additional map or residual evaluation.
review_flags: No inspected source fixed a canonical safeguard predicate or supported this family-level definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Anderson update
Damped Anderson Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A damped Anderson method scales the entire Anderson displacement by a factor between zero and one, recovering the ordinary proposal when the factor equals one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k^{AA}\) be any Anderson proposal computed from \(x_k\) and its retained history. Given a damping parameter \(\lambda_k\in(0,1]\), set
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+\lambda_k(z_k^{AA}-x_k).\]
Equivalently, if the proposal has Type-II form \(z_k^{AA}=x_k+f_k-(\Delta X_k+\Delta F_k)\gamma_k\), then
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+\lambda_k\{f_k-(\Delta X_k+\Delta F_k)\gamma_k\}.\]
The undamped variant is recovered at \(\lambda_k=1\); a prescribed lower bound \(\lambda_k\geq\lambda_{\min}>0\) prevents a nonzero proposal from being suppressed completely.
assumptions_latex: An Anderson proposal \(z_k^{AA}\in\mathbb R^n\) is available.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex damping between the current iterate and an Anderson proposal.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional relaxation of an accelerated proposal
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The stated relaxation is a coherent algorithm and fits the damped-variant leaf, but Anderson literature uses more than one damping or mixing convention. An Anderson-specific source is required to establish this exact whole-displacement convention as the intended variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Anderson Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The safeguarded method accepts a damped Anderson proposal only after verified residual decrease; otherwise it executes a designated base fixed-point step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=g(x)-x\), let \(z_k^{AA}\) be an Anderson proposal, and let \(z_k^{B}=x_k+\beta_k f(x_k)\) be a base proposal. Fix \(c\in(0,1)\) and test damping values \(\lambda\in\{1,\tau,\tau^2,\ldots\}\), where \(\tau\in(0,1)\). Accept the first \(z_k(\lambda)=x_k+\lambda(z_k^{AA}-x_k)\) satisfying
\[\|f(z_k(\lambda))\|_2\leq(1-c\lambda)\|f(x_k)\|_2.\]
If no tested value above a prescribed minimum is accepted, set \(x_{k+1}=z_k^{B}\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=z_k(\lambda)\).
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is evaluable at trial points.
A finite minimum tested damping value is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either an accepted residual-decreasing Anderson trial or the fallback proposal \(z_k^{B}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-decrease safeguard with fallback to a base fixed-point step.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is internally coherent and fits a safeguarded-variant container, but the residual Armijo test, geometric damping sequence, minimum damping rule, and fallback choice constitute a specific globalization design. No source supports this particular combination.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Activation Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one fixed finite set of tested damping factors, full acceptance occurs when the unit trial passes, damped acceptance occurs when the unit trial fails but a smaller tested factor passes, and fallback occurs when every tested factor fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_k=\|f(x_k)\|_2\), define \(z_k(\lambda)=x_k+\lambda(z_k^{AA}-x_k)\), fix \(c\in(0,1)\), and let \(\Lambda_k\subset(0,1]\) be a finite nonempty tested damping set containing \(1\). Define \(A_k(\lambda)\) by
\[A_k(\lambda)\iff \|f(z_k(\lambda))\|_2\leq(1-c\lambda)r_k.\]
The safeguard regimes are
\[\begin{aligned}
&\text{inactive: }&&A_k(1),\\
&\text{damping-active: }&&\neg A_k(1)\ \text{and}\ \exists\lambda\in\Lambda_k\setminus\{1\}:A_k(\lambda),\\
&\text{fallback-active: }&&\forall\lambda\in\Lambda_k:\neg A_k(\lambda).
\end{aligned}\]
Relative to \(\Lambda_k\), these predicates are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
assumptions_latex: The residual is evaluable at every trial point associated with \(\Lambda_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of the inactive, damping-active, or fallback-active regimes holds relative to \(\Lambda_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-way activation predicate for accepting, damping, or rejecting an Anderson proposal.

notation.meaning: finite set of damping factors tested at iteration k
acceptance predicate for a tested damping factor

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exhaustive classification induced by the stated acceptance test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Anderson history-management rule
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\), \(y_i=r(x_{i+1})-r(x_i)\), and let \(\mathcal P_k=\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\) be the indices of all available completed differences at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic selection, deletion, truncation, and restart policies for the history used in Anderson least-squares subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An Anderson history-management variant is a rule \(\mathcal M_k\) that selects an ordered index set \(I_k=\mathcal M_k(\{s_i,y_i\}_{i\in\mathcal P_k})\subseteq\mathcal P_k\), constructs \(S_k=[s_i]_{i\in I_k}\) and \(Y_k=[y_i]_{i\in I_k}\), and uses only these columns in the Anderson coefficient or multisecant problem. The rule may impose a memory bound \(|I_k|\leq m\), a numerical-rank condition such as \(\sigma_{\min}(Y_k)\geq\tau_k\), or a conditioning bound \(\kappa(Y_k)\leq K_k\). A restart is the assignment \(I_k=\varnothing\); truncation deletes selected columns; sliding-window management retains the most recent admissible indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: History management is the explicit rule selecting which past step and residual-difference pairs enter Anderson's current least-squares problem. It includes bounded windows, rank-revealing deletion, conditioning-based pruning, and complete restart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[I_k\subseteq\{0,\ldots,k-1\},\qquad S_k=[s_i]_{i\in I_k},\qquad Y_k=[y_i]_{i\in I_k},\qquad |I_k|\leq m\ \text{when a memory bound is imposed}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Selecting residual columns in the affine-coefficient formulation is equivalent to selecting the corresponding columns of \(S_k\) and \(Y_k\) in the multisecant formulation.
special_cases_latex: A depth-\(m\) sliding window uses \(I_k=\{\max(0,k-m),\ldots,k-1\}\).
A full restart uses \(I_k=\varnothing\), reducing the next update to its zero-history form.
immediate_consequences_latex: A fixed memory bound limits the Anderson least-squares problem to at most \(m\) history columns.
Deleting dependent columns can make the retained least-squares representation identifiable.
boundary_notes: Different rank tests and deletion orders generally produce different iterates.
History management is distinct from accepting or rejecting the candidate after it has been computed.

notation.meaning: Ordered set of retained history indices.

review_flags: No inspected source supplied a canonical formal taxonomy of Anderson history-management variants.
knowledge_statements.title: Anderson history-management rule
Truncated Anderson Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated Anderson applies the usual least-squares update using no more than the latest fixed number of iterate and residual differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a memory bound \(m\geq0\). At iteration \(k\), set \(m_k=\min\{m,k\}\) and retain only the pairs indexed by \(j=k-m_k,\ldots,k-1\). Form \(\Delta X_k\) and \(\Delta F_k\) from these pairs, compute \(\gamma_k=\Delta F_k^{\dagger}f(x_k)\), and set
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta_kf(x_k)-(\Delta X_k+\beta_k\Delta F_k)\gamma_k.\]
After producing \(x_{k+1}\), discard every pair older than the most recent \(m\). Hence the least-squares problem has at most \(m\) columns and history storage is at most \(2mn\) scalars.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update uses \(m_k\leq m\) secant pairs and stores at most \(2mn\) history scalars.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-memory Anderson acceleration retaining only the most recent secant pairs.

notation.meaning: history length used at iteration k

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The limited-memory algorithm fits the truncated-variant leaf and is mathematically coherent. An Anderson-specific source is still required, particularly for the exact Type-II formulation and the storage claim, which counts only the two history matrices and omits implementation-dependent auxiliary storage.

knowledge_statements.title: Restarted Anderson Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restarted variant erases all history when a trigger fires, takes a base step, and rebuilds Anderson secant information from subsequent iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Maintain a history \(\mathcal H_k\) of at most \(m\) secant pairs and a Boolean restart predicate \(R_k\). If \(R_k\) is true, replace \(\mathcal H_k\) by the empty history before computing the next step and set
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta_k f(x_k).\]
If \(R_k\) is false, form \(\Delta X_k,\Delta F_k\) from \(\mathcal H_k\), compute \(\gamma_k=\Delta F_k^{\dagger}f(x_k)\), and apply the Type-II Anderson update. Append the newly generated secant pair afterward, truncating only if its addition makes the history exceed \(m\).
assumptions_latex: A Boolean restart predicate \(R_k\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(R_k\) holds, the next update is history-free; otherwise the retained history supplies the Anderson correction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anderson acceleration with event-triggered deletion of all accumulated secant history.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard event-triggered history restart mechanism
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the restarted-variant leaf, but forcing a base step whenever the predicate fires and appending the newly generated pair afterward are particular restart semantics rather than a universal definition. A source specifying this policy is required.

knowledge_statements.title: History Reset Criteria
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset history when residual differences are numerically rank deficient, the accelerated proposal is rejected, or the prescribed restart period expires.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q_k\) count iterations since the last reset, let \(a_k\in\{0,1\}\) indicate acceptance of the Anderson proposal, and let \(\sigma_{\min}^{+}(\Delta F_k)\) denote the smallest positive singular value. For thresholds \(\varepsilon_{m rank}>0\) and an integer \(p\geq1\), define
\[R_k=\bigl[\sigma_{\min}^{+}(\Delta F_k)\leq\varepsilon_{m rank}\|\Delta F_k\|_2\bigr]\ \lor\ [a_k=0]\ \lor\ [q_k\geq p].\]
If \(\Delta F_k\) has no positive singular value, the first clause is declared true. A history reset is executed exactly when \(R_k\) is true.
assumptions_latex: The acceptance indicator \(a_k\) and counter \(q_k\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Boolean predicate completely determines whether the history is reset at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete reset predicate combining ill-conditioning, failed acceptance, and periodic restart.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit implementable union of common restart triggers
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the reset-criteria leaf, and the Boolean predicate is implementable. Nevertheless, the union of numerical-rank, rejection, and periodic triggers is a bespoke design template; no citation supports this exact criterion or its thresholds as an established Anderson reset policy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Anderson–multisecant–Krylov correspondence
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G(x)=Ax+b\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), let \(M=I-A\), and let \(f(x)=Mx-b=x-G(x)\). Assume exact arithmetic, undamped Anderson acceleration, and no truncation or breakdown through the iteration being compared.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear affine fixed-point maps with full history; nonlinear, restarted, damped, and finite-precision cases are excluded from the exact correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Anderson multisecant–Krylov correspondence is the identification, for an affine map, of three descriptions of the same residual-minimizing construction: Anderson coefficients form an affine combination of previous iterates minimizing the norm of the combined residual; the associated inverse model satisfies accumulated multisecant equations \(H_kY_k=S_k\); and the residual search is over the Krylov space \(\mathcal K_k(M,f(x_0))=\operatorname{span}\{f(x_0),Mf(x_0),\ldots,M^{k-1}f(x_0)\}\). Under the stated nonbreakdown conventions, the Anderson iterate corresponds to the residual-minimizing GMRES iterate, up to the conventional shift between the extrapolated point and its subsequent fixed-point image.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear affine fixed-point map and full undamped history, Anderson residual minimization can be described equivalently through accumulated inverse multisecant equations and through residual minimization over a Krylov space. With compatible indexing and no breakdown, this is the GMRES construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal K_k(M,f_0)=\operatorname{span}\{f_0,Mf_0,\ldots,M^{k-1}f_0\},\qquad H_kY_k=S_k,\qquad \|f(x_k)\|_2=\min_{x\in x_0+\mathcal K_k(M,f_0)}\|Mx-b\|_2,\] with the final equality subject to the stated Anderson/GMRES indexing convention.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For affine \(f\), residual differences satisfy \(y_i=f(x_{i+1})-f(x_i)=Ms_i\), so the multisecant equations reproduce the action of \(M^{-1}\) on retained residual differences.
The affine Anderson least-squares problem and a Krylov residual-minimization problem have the same linear-algebraic data when full history is retained.
special_cases_latex: If the initial residual is zero, both methods terminate immediately.
A restart replaces the full Krylov space by a restarted subspace and destroys the unrestricted full-history identity.
immediate_consequences_latex: Linear dependence or stagnation must be handled consistently on both sides of the correspondence.
boundary_notes: The correspondence is not an exact GMRES equivalence for a general nonlinear map.
Damping, regularization, truncation, and finite precision can change the compared iterates.
review_flags: An authoritative source is required to settle the precise Anderson/GMRES indexing, nonstagnation hypotheses, and iterate-versus-image convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Anderson–multisecant–Krylov correspondence
Multisecant Interpretation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type-II Anderson can be represented as a quasi-Newton step whose inverse-Jacobian model satisfies all retained residual-to-iterate secant equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), let \(\Delta X_k,\Delta F_k\) contain retained secant differences, and assume \(\Delta F_k\) has full column rank. For \(\beta_k>0\), define
\[H_k=-\beta_k I+(\Delta X_k+\beta_k\Delta F_k)(\Delta F_k^{T}\Delta F_k)^{-1}\Delta F_k^{T}.\]
Then \(H_k\Delta F_k=\Delta X_k\), so \(H_k\) satisfies every retained inverse multisecant equation, and the step \(x_{k+1}=x_k-H_kF(x_k)\) equals
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta_kF(x_k)-(\Delta X_k+\beta_k\Delta F_k)(\Delta F_k^{T}\Delta F_k)^{-1}\Delta F_k^{T}F(x_k).\]
This is the full-column-rank Type-II Anderson formula for the residual convention \(F=g-I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_k\Delta F_k=\Delta X_k\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k-H_kF(x_k)\) is the corresponding Type-II Anderson update.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-II Anderson represented as an inverse-Jacobian multisecant step.

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.5 Quasi-Newton Methods p. 59

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Interpretation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear fixed-point problem without stagnation, full-memory unit-mixing Anderson uses the same residual-minimizing Krylov affine combination as GMRES.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)=Ax+b\), set \(M=I-A\), and assume \(M\) is nonsingular. Starting from \(x_0\), unrestarted full-history Anderson acceleration with unit mixing produces coefficients whose affine combination \(\bar x_k\) minimizes \(\|b-Mx\|_2\) over
\[x_0+\mathcal K_k(M,r_0),\qquad \mathcal K_k(M,r_0)=\operatorname{span}\{r_0,Mr_0,\ldots,M^{k-1}r_0\},\quad r_0=b-Mx_0,\]
provided the residual-difference least-squares problems do not stagnate. Thus \(\bar x_k\) is the corresponding GMRES iterate and the Anderson output satisfies \(x_{k+1}=g(\bar x_k)\).
assumptions_latex: Anderson uses full history and unit mixing.
No least-squares or GMRES stagnation occurs before iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_k\) is the GMRES minimizer over \(x_0+\mathcal K_k(I-A,r_0)\), and \(x_{k+1}=g(\bar x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear fixed-point Anderson iterates represented through GMRES residual minimization.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the Krylov-interpretation leaf, and the hypotheses appropriately limit the claim to linear, full-history, unit-mixing, nonstagnating iterations. The cited generic Krylov chapter does not support the specific Anderson–GMRES equivalence, indexing, or affine-precursor formula; a direct authoritative source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Multisecant–Krylov Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On linear problems, Anderson’s least-squares Krylov minimization and its inverse multisecant model describe the same history-generated correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(g(x)=Ax+b\), let \(M=I-A\) be nonsingular and \(r(x)=b-Mx\). With full history, unit mixing, and no stagnation, the Anderson history obeys \(\Delta r_k=-M\Delta X_k\). The Type-II least-squares coefficient minimizes
\[\|r(x_k)-\Delta r_k\gamma\|_2,\]
while the associated inverse model satisfies \(H_k\Delta r_k=\Delta X_k\). Because the columns of \(\Delta X_k\) lie in \(\mathcal K_k(M,r_0)\), these are respectively the residual-minimization and multisecant descriptions of the same history-generated correction. The resulting affine precursor is the GMRES iterate, and applying \(g\) yields the Anderson iterate.
assumptions_latex: Full history and unit mixing are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Anderson correction has both a multisecant representation and a GMRES Krylov residual-minimization representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-problem correspondence between multisecant inverse actions and Krylov residual minimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Extrapolation Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear extrapolator forms a data-dependent affine combination of recent iterates, preserves constant sequences, and may place the estimate outside their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(m\ge 1\). For a window \(X_k=(x_{k-m},\ldots,x_k)\in(\mathbb R^n)^{m+1}\), a nonlinear extrapolation rule is a map \(\mathcal E_m:(\mathbb R^n)^{m+1}\to\mathbb R^n\) of the form \[\mathcal E_m(X_k)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}\alpha_j(X_k)x_{k-m+j},\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{m}\alpha_j(X_k)=1,\] where the coefficient map \(X_k\mapsto(\alpha_0(X_k),\ldots,\alpha_m(X_k))\) is data-dependent and generally nonlinear. The affine constraint gives constant-sequence consistency, \(\mathcal E_m(x,\ldots,x)=x\). Applied to \(x_{i+1}=G(x_i)\), the vector \(\mathcal E_m(X_k)\) is the extrapolated fixed-point estimate; it is strictly extrapolative whenever it lies outside \(\operatorname{conv}\{x_{k-m},\ldots,x_k\}\).
assumptions_latex: The coefficient functions \(\alpha_j\) are defined on the iterate window under consideration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Data-dependent affine-combination formulation for accelerating vector fixed-point sequences.

notation.meaning: Window of the most recent m+1 iterates.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly addresses nonlinear extrapolation methods.
The affine-combination sense should be checked against the intended taxonomy scope.
standard_field_rationale: data-dependent affine extrapolation with constant preservation is a standard vector-sequence formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear sequence extrapolation method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional vector space, let \(x_0,x_1,\ldots\in X\) be generated by an underlying iteration, and let \(m_k\geq1\) specify the available window \(x_{k-m_k},\ldots,x_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector-sequence transformations that construct a new approximation from a finite history; no single coefficient-selection functional is imposed on the whole family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear extrapolation method is a sequence transformation \(E_k:X^{m_k+1}\to X\) producing \(z_k=E_k(x_{k-m_k},\ldots,x_k)\), where the transformation is designed to eliminate or reduce components of a local error model inferred from the finite history. In an affine extrapolation variant, \(z_k=\sum_{j=0}^{m_k}\alpha_{k,j}x_{k-m_k+j}\) with \(\sum_j\alpha_{k,j}=1\), and the coefficients are determined from difference, residual, interpolation, or minimal-norm conditions. Translation covariance, \(E_k(x_0+c,\\ldots,x_m+c)=E_k(x_0,\ldots,x_m)+c\), is ensured by the affine coefficient constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear extrapolation method transforms a finite window of an iterative sequence into a new approximation intended to cancel modeled error components. In the common affine form, it combines the window with coefficients summing to one and obtains those coefficients from explicit difference, residual, interpolation, or norm-minimization conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When coefficients sum to one, \(z_k\) may be written as the newest iterate plus a linear combination of successive differences.
An extrapolated point may either replace the base iterate or be used only as a predictor for a subsequent correction.
special_cases_latex: Scalar sequence transformations arise when \(X=\mathbb R\).
Minimal polynomial and reduced-rank extrapolation are obtained from particular linear conditions on successive differences.
immediate_consequences_latex: Affine extrapolation is invariant under translation of every point in the history by the same vector.
boundary_notes: The family definition does not guarantee that \(z_k\) is closer to a limit.
Anderson acceleration is distinguished by its fixed-point residual least-squares construction and use of mapped points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Higher-order methods adapted to singular roots
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be sufficiently differentiable near \(x_*\), with \(F(x_*)=0\) and singular Jacobian \(J_*=F'(x_*)\), so \(\operatorname{rank}J_*<n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local deterministic equation-solving methods whose models explicitly address Jacobian singularity or root multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A singular-root higher-order method constructs \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\) from a model \(M_k(p)\) that contains information beyond the ordinary nonsingular Newton equation \(F(x_k)+F'(x_k)p=0\), and whose defining equations explicitly use higher derivatives, multiplicity data, null-space information, deflation, or interpolation conditions to resolve directions in which \(F'(x_*)\) is singular. A tensor-model member uses \(M_k(p)=F(x_k)+F'(x_k)p+\tfrac12T_k[p,p]\); a multiplicity-aware scalar member rescales the Newton correction using the root multiplicity. Merely applying unmodified Newton iteration to a singular root does not by itself define a member of the adapted family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family consists of local root solvers that modify the ordinary Newton model specifically because the derivative at the root is singular. The modification may use higher-order tensors, multiplicity information, null-space equations, deflation, or interpolation so that missing first-order information is supplied by additional structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F(x_*)=0,\quad \operatorname{rank}F'(x_*)<n,\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k,\quad p_k\ \text{is defined by a singularity-adapted higher-order or augmented model}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Jacobian singularity means \(\ker F'(x_*)\neq\{0\}\); adapted models supply conditions governing at least part of this null space.
special_cases_latex: Tensor models add quadratic or higher multilinear terms.
For a scalar root of known multiplicity, modified Newton iteration multiplies the Newton correction by that multiplicity.
immediate_consequences_latex: The defining model can remain informative along directions annihilated by the limiting Jacobian.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert a particular local order for every member.
Methods for nonsingular simple roots are outside this slot unless explicitly specialized to singularity.

notation.meaning: Action of a second-order tensor on the step twice.

review_flags: The inspected tensor-method source supports one subfamily but not this broader singular-root higher-order family definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-order methods adapted to singular roots
Tensor Methods near Singular Roots
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a quadratic Taylor model of the residual, optionally inside a trust region, so curvature supplies information along directions where the Jacobian is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a twice continuously differentiable map \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and an iterate \(x_k\), form the quadratic residual model \[T_k(s)=F(x_k)+F'(x_k)s+\tfrac12F''(x_k)[s,s].\] Compute a step \(s_k\) that approximately minimizes \(\|T_k(s)\|_2\), subject when necessary to \(\|s\|_2\leq\Delta_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) after an acceptance test based on actual versus predicted residual reduction. Stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|_2\leq\varepsilon\). Retaining the tensor term permits model reduction along directions in or near \(\ker F'(x_k)\), where the ordinary Newton equation may be singular or ineffective.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic model subproblem is solved to a prescribed residual or stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), where \(s_k\) exploits both \(F'(x_k)\) and \(F''(x_k)\) near a singular root.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order tensor-model iteration for a square residual system with a rank-deficient or ill-conditioned Jacobian.

notation.meaning: second-order Taylor model of the residual at the current iterate
bilinear second derivative of the residual map

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but no cited source supports this particular quadratic-residual trust-region formulation or the claim that retaining the tensor term supplies useful reduction near the Jacobian kernel. An authoritative tensor-method source with a specific algorithm, section, or page locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interpolatory tensor method for nonlinear equations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be differentiable, let \(J(x)=r'(x)\), and let \(x_k\) be the current iterate. For a third-order tensor \(T_k\), define \((T_kuv)_i=\sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{\ell=1}^n(T_k)_{ij\ell}u_jv_\ell\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional tensor models for nonlinear systems, particularly degenerate roots with Jacobian rank \(n-1\) or \(n-2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tensor method replaces the Newton linear model by \(\widehat M_k(p)=r(x_k)+J(x_k)p+\tfrac12T_kpp\). In the low-storage interpolatory form, \(T_k\) is chosen so that \(\widehat M_k(x_{k-j}-x_k)=r(x_{k-j})\) for \(j=1,\ldots,q\). The step is a solution of \(\widehat M_k(p)=0\) when one is selected, or a minimizer of \(\|\widehat M_k(p)\|_2^2\) when the tensor equation has no chosen exact solution. The model is intended to capture nonlinear behavior omitted by Newton's linear model and is especially directed at degenerate roots.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tensor method augments the Newton residual model with a quadratic tensor term. In its interpolatory form, the tensor is chosen to reproduce residual values at selected previous iterates. The next step solves the tensor model or minimizes its squared residual when an exact model root is unavailable.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(s_{jk}=x_{k-j}-x_k\), interpolation is equivalent to \(\tfrac12T_ks_{jk}s_{jk}=r(x_{k-j})-r(x_k)-J(x_k)s_{jk}\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing \((T_k)_{ij\ell}=[\nabla^2r_i(x_k)]_{j\ell}\) gives the exact second-derivative quadratic Taylor model.
Taking \(T_k=0\) reduces the model to Newton's linear model.
immediate_consequences_latex: The interpolatory model exactly reproduces each retained residual value at its corresponding historical displacement.
boundary_notes: An exact tensor-model root need not exist.
The full exact tensor requires cubic-scale storage; low-storage interpolatory representations restrict its form.

notation.meaning: Third-order tensor defining the quadratic vector term.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scalar Householder root iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:I\to\mathbb R\) be sufficiently differentiable on an interval \(I\), let \(x_k\in I\) satisfy \(f(x_k)\neq0\), and let \(d\geq1\) be an integer such that the required derivatives of \(1/f\) exist and the denominator below is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical scalar Householder family; multivariate higher-order Newton constructions require separate tensor or multilinear definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Householder method indexed by \(d\geq1\) is the scalar root iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d\,[(1/f)^{(d-1)}(x_k)]/[(1/f)^{(d)}(x_k)]\). The update is defined only where \(f(x_k)\neq0\) and \((1/f)^{(d)}(x_k)\neq0\); if \(f(x_k)=0\), the root has already been reached. The member \(d=1\) is Newton's method, while \(d=2\) is Halley's method after algebraic simplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a scalar equation, the Householder family updates \(x_k\) using the ratio of two successive derivatives of the reciprocal function \(1/f\), multiplied by the integer index \(d\). Newton and Halley iterations are its first two members.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(d=1\), the formula becomes \(x_{k+1}=x_k-f(x_k)/f'(x_k)\).
For \(d=2\), it becomes \(x_{k+1}=x_k-2f(x_k)f'(x_k)/(2f'(x_k)^2-f(x_k)f''(x_k))\).
special_cases_latex: \(d=1\) is Newton iteration.
\(d=2\) is Halley iteration.
immediate_consequences_latex: Each increase in \(d\) requires one additional derivative of \(1/f\), or equivalent derivative information from \(f\).
boundary_notes: The formula is undefined at a nonterminated iterate if its denominator vanishes.
The usual high local order requires a sufficiently smooth function and a simple root; those convergence hypotheses are not part of this definition.
Householder root iteration is unrelated to Householder orthogonal reflections used in QR factorization.

notation.meaning: The \(j\)-th derivative of the reciprocal function \(x\mapsto1/f(x)\).

review_flags: The inspected sources did not provide the classical reciprocal-derivative Householder formula with a precise locator.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Householder root iteration
Higher-Order Newton Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a degree-p Taylor model of the residual at each iterate; near a simple root, the exact local branch can attain order p+1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\geq1\). For \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), define at \(x_k\) the order-\(p\) Taylor model \[T_{p,k}(s)=\sum_{j=0}^{p}\frac{1}{j!}F^{(j)}(x_k)[s]^j.\] Choose a locally small solution or approximate solution \(s_k\) of \(T_{p,k}(s)=0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), and stop when the residual or step meets a prescribed tolerance. When \(p=1\), the update is Newton's method. If \(F\in C^{p+1}\), the root \(x_*\) is simple, and the selected model root remains in the local branch converging to zero, the exact update has local error \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=O(\|x_k-x_*\|^{p+1})\).
assumptions_latex: The locally convergent solution branch of the Taylor equation is selected.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Taylor-model generalization of Newton iteration for smooth square nonlinear systems.

notation.meaning: jth derivative applied to j copies of the step

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the terminal method-family container, and the formulas are internally coherent. However, the multivariate Taylor-model iteration, local branch-selection hypothesis, and asserted order p+1 require an authoritative source with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Householder Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Householder's scalar update differentiates the reciprocal residual; degree d gives local order d+1 at a sufficiently smooth simple root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\geq1\) and let \(f:I\to\mathbb{R}\) be sufficiently differentiable with \(f(x_k)\neq0\). Define the Householder update \[x_{k+1}=x_k+d\,\frac{\left(1/f\right)^{(d-1)}(x_k)}{\left(1/f\right)^{(d)}(x_k)},\] whenever the denominator is nonzero, and stop when \(|f(x_k)|\leq\varepsilon\) or \(|x_{k+1}-x_k|\leq\varepsilon_x\). The case \(d=1\) is Newton's method and \(d=2\) is Halley's method. If \(x_*\) is a simple zero and the required derivatives exist near \(x_*\), then for starting points sufficiently close to \(x_*\) the method has local convergence order \(d+1\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has the derivatives required by the displayed update near a simple zero \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical scalar Householder iteration of arbitrary integer order at a simple root.

notation.meaning: Householder index; the convergence order is d+1
jth derivative of the reciprocal function

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The scalar Householder formula and algorithm role fit the leaf, but the record supplies no citation for the indexing convention, Newton and Halley special cases, or the local order d+1 result. A specifically located authoritative source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Order–Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare local order with derivative and solve costs through the efficiency index q^(1/c); a higher-order method can be less efficient if each step costs more.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose method \(M_i\) has local error relation \(e_{k+1}=C_i e_k^{q_i}+o(e_k^{q_i})\), with \(q_i>1\), and costs \(c_i>0\) normalized work units per iteration. Its classical efficiency index is \[E_i=q_i^{1/c_i}.\] Under the idealized model of constant per-iteration cost and asymptotic errors, reducing an error exponent by a factor \(R>1\) requires approximately \(\log R/\log q_i\) iterations and \(c_i\log R/\log q_i\) work units. Thus method \(M_1\) is asymptotically preferable by this metric exactly when \(q_1^{1/c_1}>q_2^{1/c_2}\); higher convergence order alone does not establish lower computational cost.
assumptions_latex: Each method has a well-defined local order \(q_i>1\).
The normalized cost \(c_i\) is constant in the asymptotic regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_1\) dominates \(M_2\) in the classical efficiency metric if and only if \(q_1^{1/c_1}>q_2^{1/c_2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Efficiency comparison for locally convergent root iterations under an explicit per-step cost model.

notation.meaning: local convergence order of method i
normalized work per iteration of method i

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property role is appropriate for an order–cost tradeoff leaf. The efficiency index and comparison are plausible under the stated idealized constant-cost model, but no source is cited for the metric or its interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicity-Aware Root Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying the Newton correction by the known root multiplicity restores quadratic convergence that ordinary Newton generally loses at a multiple scalar root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:I\to\mathbb{R}\) have a root \(x_*\) of known multiplicity \(m\geq2\). From \(x_0\) sufficiently close to \(x_*\), compute \[x_{k+1}=x_k-m\frac{f(x_k)}{f'(x_k)}\] whenever \(f'(x_k)\neq0\), and stop when \(|f(x_k)|\leq\varepsilon\) or the step is sufficiently small. If \(f(x)=(x-x_*)^m g(x)\), where \(g\in C^2\) and \(g(x_*)\neq0\), then the modified iteration is locally quadratically convergent. In contrast, the unmodified Newton update applied to the same multiple root is generally only linearly convergent, with asymptotic error factor \((m-1)/m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Modified scalar Newton iteration when the root multiplicity is known.

notation.meaning: local nonvanishing factor of the residual

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The multiplicity-corrected Newton algorithm fits the leaf and is stated for the scalar, known-multiplicity case without blending it with system variants. The quadratic rate and the unmodified Newton asymptotic factor nevertheless require a specifically located authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplicity-aware scalar root iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:I\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and let \(x_*\in I\) be a root of known integer multiplicity \(m\geq2\), meaning \(f(x)=(x-x_*)^mg(x)\) locally with \(g(x_*)\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar methods explicitly using known or estimated root multiplicity; general singular systems require deflation or null-space constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplicity-aware Newton method uses the multiplicity parameter in the correction and is defined by \(x_{k+1}=x_k-m f(x_k)/f'(x_k)\) whenever \(f'(x_k)\neq0\). More generally, a scalar root method is multiplicity-aware when its update contains a supplied or estimated multiplicity \(m_k\) and reduces to the modified Newton correction when \(m_k=m\). Equivalently, when a differentiable local factorization can be used, it applies ordinary Newton iteration to the simple-root factor \(h(x)=f(x)^{1/m}\), with a locally consistent branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a scalar root of known multiplicity \(m\), the canonical multiplicity-aware modification multiplies the Newton correction by \(m\). Locally this is equivalent to applying Newton's method to an appropriate branch of the simple-root factor \(f^{1/m}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a locally consistent branch \(h=f^{1/m}\), Newton's update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-h(x_k)/h'(x_k)\) equals \(x_k-mf(x_k)/f'(x_k)\).
Multiplicity \(m\) is equivalently characterized by \(f^{(j)}(x_*)=0\) for \(0\leq j<m\) and \(f^{(m)}(x_*)\neq0\), when these derivatives exist.
special_cases_latex: For \(m=1\), the formula is ordinary Newton iteration.
An adaptive variant replaces \(m\) by an explicitly defined estimate \(m_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The update is explicitly different from ordinary Newton iteration whenever \(m>1\) and \(f(x_k)\neq0\).
boundary_notes: A wrong multiplicity parameter changes the local iteration.
The scalar factorization does not directly define multiplicity for a general vector-valued singular root.

notation.meaning: Known algebraic multiplicity of the scalar root.
Nonvanishing local factor in the root factorization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuation and homotopy path tracking
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be the target residual and let \(H:\mathbb R^n\times[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable, with an easily known \(a\) satisfying \(H(a,0)=0\) and with \(H(x,1)=F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical continuation for general finite-dimensional nonlinear systems; polynomial solution enumeration and bifurcation classification are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuation-homotopy path-tracking method follows a connected zero path \(z(s)=(x(s),\lambda(s))\) satisfying \(H(x(s),\lambda(s))=0\), beginning at \((a,0)\) and seeking a point \((x_*,1)\). At a regular path point, the augmented derivative \([H_x\ H_\lambda]\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n+1)}\) has rank \(n\), and a unit tangent \((\dot x,\dot\lambda)\) satisfies \(H_x\dot x+H_\lambda\dot\lambda=0\) and \(\|\dot x\|_2^2+|\dot\lambda|^2=1\), with orientation chosen consistently. Numerical members integrate this tangent system or alternate tangent prediction with correction back to \(H=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuation embeds the target equation in a parameterized homotopy with a known starting solution and tracks a connected curve of homotopy zeros until the target parameter is reached. At regular points, the tangent is the oriented unit null vector of the augmented homotopy Jacobian.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The path may be tracked as an initial-value differential system for the tangent or by an algebraic predictor–corrector iteration.
A standard linear homotopy is \(H(x,\lambda)=\lambda F(x)+(1-\lambda)(x-a)\).
special_cases_latex: Natural parameter continuation uses \(\lambda\) itself as the local path parameter where \(H_x\) is nonsingular.
Arclength parameterization permits \(\lambda\) to decrease near a turning point.
immediate_consequences_latex: At \(\lambda=0\), the standard linear homotopy has the known zero \(x=a\); at \(\lambda=1\), every homotopy zero is a target-system zero.
boundary_notes: Path existence from \((a,0)\) to parameter one is not automatic.
At points where \([H_x\ H_\lambda]\) loses full row rank, the regular tangent definition is insufficient.

knowledge_statements.title: Natural Parameter Continuation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Advance the physical parameter, predict with the solution derivative, and correct at fixed parameter; the method fails as a parametrization when the state Jacobian becomes singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and suppose \(F(x_k,\lambda_k)=0\). Choose \(h_k\), set \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+h_k\), and compute the tangent predictor from \[F_x(x_k,\lambda_k)\dot{x}_k=-F_\lambda(x_k,\lambda_k),\qquad x_{k+1}^{(0)}=x_k+h_k\dot{x}_k.\] Correct at fixed \(\lambda_{k+1}\) by Newton iterations \[F_x(x_{k+1}^{(j)},\lambda_{k+1})\delta x^{(j)}=-F(x_{k+1}^{(j)},\lambda_{k+1}),\qquad x_{k+1}^{(j+1)}=x_{k+1}^{(j)}+\delta x^{(j)}.\] Accept the corrected point when its residual meets tolerance. This parametrization is locally valid only while \(F_x\) remains nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: \(F\in C^1\) near the tracked solution curve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted point approximates a solution of \(F(x,\lambda_{k+1})=0\) on the local graph \(x=x(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuation using the physical parameter itself as the local path coordinate.

notation.meaning: derivative of the solution with respect to the parameter

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Natural-parameter continuation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb R^n\times[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable and suppose \(H(x_0,\lambda_0)=0\). On a path segment, assume \(H_x(x,\lambda)\) is nonsingular so that the zero set can locally be represented as \(x=x(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular continuation segments parameterized directly by the problem parameter; turning points requiring arclength reparameterization are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Natural-parameter continuation treats \(\lambda\) as the independent path variable and follows a function \(x(\lambda)\) satisfying \(H(x(\lambda),\lambda)=0\). Its tangent is defined by \(x'(\lambda)=-H_x(x(\lambda),\lambda)^{-1}H_\lambda(x(\lambda),\lambda)\). A discrete predictor–corrector member chooses \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\Delta\lambda_k\), predicts \(x_{k+1}^{P}=x_k+\Delta\lambda_k x'(\lambda_k)\), and corrects \(x\) at fixed \(\lambda_{k+1}\) until \(H(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Natural-parameter continuation uses the homotopy parameter itself as the path coordinate. Where the Jacobian with respect to \(x\) is invertible, it differentiates or predicts the solution as a function of \(\lambda\), then solves the homotopy equation at the new fixed parameter value.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A zero-order predictor sets \(x_{k+1}^{P}=x_k\) and corrects at the new parameter.
For \(H(x,\lambda)=\lambda F(x)+(1-\lambda)(x-a)\), increasing \(\lambda\) from zero to one transforms the easy equation \(x-a=0\) into \(F(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: Fixed-step continuation uses constant \(\Delta\lambda_k\).
Adaptive natural continuation changes \(\Delta\lambda_k\) while retaining \(\lambda\) as the independent variable.
immediate_consequences_latex: If continuation reaches \(\lambda=1\) and \(H(x,1)=F(x)\), the corrected point solves \(F(x)=0\).
boundary_notes: The representation \(x=x(\lambda)\) fails at a turning point where \(H_x\) becomes singular.
Natural-parameter continuation cannot follow a branch requiring local reversal of \(\lambda\) without reparameterization.

notation.meaning: Predicted solution at the next parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Arclength Continuation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predict along the solution tangent and correct on a transverse hyperplane, allowing the path to pass a generic fold where natural-parameter continuation fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z=(x,\lambda)\) and let \(F(x,\lambda)=0\) define a one-dimensional solution curve. Given a corrected point \(z_k\), a unit tangent \(t_k\in\ker [F_x(z_k)\;F_\lambda(z_k)]\), and step \(h_k\), predict \(z_{k+1}^{(0)}=z_k+h_k t_k\). Correct by Newton's method applied to \[G_k(z)=\begin{pmatrix}F(x,\lambda)\\ t_k^{\mathsf T}(z-z_{k+1}^{(0)})\end{pmatrix}=0.\] Accept when both the residual and hyperplane constraint satisfy tolerance, then recompute and orient the tangent so that \(t_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}t_k>0\). The method is locally well posed whenever the augmented Jacobian \(G_k'(z)\) is nonsingular, including at a generic fold where \(F_x\) is singular.
assumptions_latex: \(F\in C^1\) and its zero set is locally a regular one-dimensional curve.
The augmented corrector Jacobian is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The corrector returns a nearby point satisfying both \(F(x,\lambda)=0\) and the pseudo-arclength hyperplane equation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Augmented continuation that remains regular through a generic fold of the natural parameter.

notation.meaning: oriented unit tangent to the solution curve

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pseudo-Arclength Continuation Step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, write \(z=(x,\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\), and suppose \(F(z_k)=0\). Let \(t_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) be a unit tangent satisfying \(D F(z_k)t_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth continuation of a locally one-dimensional solution set; the definition permits folds in the distinguished parameter but excludes branch points where the augmented corrector is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Pseudo-arclength continuation with signed step \(h_k\neq0\) first forms \(z_k^{\mathrm p}=z_k+h_kt_k\), then defines the corrected point \(z_{k+1}\) as a solution of
\[
F(z_{k+1})=0,\qquad t_k^{T}(z_{k+1}-z_k)-h_k=0.
\]
Equivalently, \(z_{k+1}\) is a zero of the square augmented residual \(G_k(z)=(F(z),\,t_k^T(z-z_k)-h_k)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\). The scalar constraint locally parameterizes the solution curve by displacement along its tangent rather than by \(\lambda\). An orientation convention, such as \(t_k^Tt_{k-1}>0\), fixes the sign of successive tangents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth equation family \(F(x,\lambda)=0\), pseudo-arclength continuation predicts along a normalized null vector of the extended Jacobian and corrects by solving the original equations together with one tangent-hyperplane equation. Thus each corrected point satisfies both \(F(z_{k+1})=0\) and \(t_k^T(z_{k+1}-z_k)=h_k\). The continuation coordinate is the signed tangent displacement, not the physical parameter \(\lambda\), so an ordinary fold where \(d\lambda/ds=0\) need not stop the path.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The corrector hyperplane can be written \(t_k^T(z-z_k^{\mathrm p})=0\), because \(z_k^{\mathrm p}=z_k+h_kt_k\) and \(\|t_k\|_2=1\).
A tangent update at a regular corrected point may be defined by \(D F(z_{k+1})t_{k+1}=0\), \(\|t_{k+1}\|_2=1\), and an orientation condition \(t_{k+1}^Tt_k>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(D_xF\) is nonsingular and \(\lambda\) is locally monotone, the same branch can also be parameterized by \(\lambda\); pseudo-arclength then differs only in the chosen local coordinate.
immediate_consequences_latex: At a simple fold, \(D_xF\) may be singular while the augmented Jacobian \(\begin{pmatrix}D F(z)\\t_k^T\end{pmatrix}\) remains nonsingular, allowing a locally well-defined corrector.
boundary_notes: No inspected local source supplied a precise pseudo-arclength definition, so the mathematical candidate requires independent source verification.
At branch points the nullspace of \(D F\) may have dimension greater than one; branch switching requires additional choices not included here.

Predictor–Corrector Path Tracking
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track a regular zero curve by predicting along its tangent, correcting on a transverse hyperplane, and adapting the step according to corrector performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) have a regular zero curve and let \(z_k\) satisfy \(H(z_k)=0\). Compute an oriented unit tangent \(t_k\) from \[H'(z_k)t_k=0,\qquad \|t_k\|_2=1,\qquad t_k^{\mathsf T}t_{k-1}>0.\] Choose a step \(h_k>0\) and predict \(z_{k+1}^{(0)}=z_k+h_k t_k\). Correct the predictor by solving \[H(z)=0,\qquad t_k^{\mathsf T}(z-z_{k+1}^{(0)})=0\] to prescribed tolerances. Accept the corrected point, reduce \(h_k\) after correction failure, and optionally enlarge it after rapid convergence. Stop at the requested endpoint, event, or step limit.
assumptions_latex: \(H'(z)\) has rank \(n\) along the tracked segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted \(z_{k+1}\) approximates the same regular component of \(H^{-1}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic tangent-prediction and transverse-correction scheme for a regular residual path.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predictor–Corrector Tracking of an Implicit Solution Path
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable and let \(z:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) parameterize a regular branch with \(H(z(s))=0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}D H(z(s))=n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth tracking of a regular one-dimensional implicit path. The definition covers natural-parameter and arclength correctors but not singular branch selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A predictor–corrector path tracker is an iteration that, from an accepted point \(z_k\in H^{-1}(0)\), constructs a predictor
\[
z_k^{\mathrm p}=z_k+h_kt_k+e_k^{\mathrm p},\qquad D H(z_k)t_k=0,
\]
where \(h_k\) is a chosen step and \(e_k^{\mathrm p}\) is the predictor truncation error, and then computes an accepted correction \(z_{k+1}\) satisfying
\[
H(z_{k+1})=0,\qquad C_k(z_{k+1})=0,
\]
for a scalar local parameterization constraint \(C_k\), with \(z_{k+1}\) selected near \(z_k^{\mathrm p}\). The corrector is commonly realized as Newton iteration on the square residual \((H,C_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predictor–corrector tracking alternates two mathematically distinct operations. The predictor extrapolates from a known point on the implicit branch, usually along a tangent satisfying \(D H(z_k)t_k=0\). The corrector then returns the prediction to the branch by solving \(H(z)=0\) together with one scalar equation \(C_k(z)=0\) that chooses a unique nearby point. A step is accepted only as the corrected point; prediction error and nonlinear-correction convergence may be used to choose the next step size.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For natural-parameter correction, one may take \(C_k(x,\lambda)=\lambda-\lambda_{k+1}^{\mathrm p}\).
For pseudo-arclength correction, one may take \(C_k(z)=t_k^T(z-z_k^{\mathrm p})\).
special_cases_latex: A zeroth-order predictor uses \(z_k^{\mathrm p}=z_k\); a tangent predictor uses \(z_k^{\mathrm p}=z_k+h_kt_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: When the augmented Jacobian \(\begin{pmatrix}D H(z_{k+1})\\D C_k(z_{k+1})\end{pmatrix}\) is nonsingular, the chosen corrector defines an isolated nearby corrected point.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a particular nonlinear solver, error estimator, or step-size controller.
No inspected local source supported this exact general predictor–corrector formulation; a precise continuation reference is required.

notation.meaning: Scalar corrector constraint selecting a nearby point on the path.

Alternatively, at a current zero (x,\lambda) with tangent (\dot{x},\dot{\lambda}), form (x^P,\lambda^P)=(x,\lambda)+\epsilon(\dot{x},\dot{\lambda}), and apply corrector iterations to obtain (x^+,\lambda^+) satisfying H(x^+,\lambda^+)=0. During correction, hold fixed a predictor component selected among those that have changed most rapidly over recent steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero path can be followed either by integrating its tangent differential equation from the known initial zero or by taking a tangent predictor step and correcting the result back to the path. In the predictor–corrector variant, a rapidly changing component is held fixed during correction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-component bordered Newton correction and its rank boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A corrector subroutine within general predictor–corrector homotopy tracking; the fixed component may change between continuation steps, particularly near a turning point in the parameter coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a corrector iterate, choose i\in\{1,\ldots,n+1\} and compute (\delta x,\delta\lambda) from \begin{bmatrix}H_x&H_\lambda\\e_i^T\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\delta x\\\delta\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-H\\0\end{bmatrix}, with H, H_x, and H_\lambda evaluated at the latest corrector point. The last row enforces e_i^T(\delta x,\delta\lambda)=0 and therefore fixes the selected component during correction. Near a turning point in \lambda, fixing an x-component instead of \lambda may be more appropriate. The described path-following variants require [H_x\;H_\lambda] to have full row rank along the path so that the tangent is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The corrector solves a bordered Newton system whose final row fixes one selected component of the correction. The component can change between steps, and an x-component may be preferable near a turning point in the parameter. The path trackers rely on full row rank of the augmented homotopy derivative for a well-defined tangent.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is differentiable at the current corrector point}
\operatorname{rank}[H_x\;H_\lambda]=n\text{ along the tracked path for tangent-based path following}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Jacobian-Based Taxonomy of Continuation Singularities
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, let \(z_*=(x_*,\lambda_*)\) satisfy \(F(z_*)=0\), and write \(A=D_xF(z_*)\) and \(B=D_{(x,\lambda)}F(z_*)=[A\;F_\lambda(z_*)]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local, finite-dimensional, one-parameter classification by ranks and tangent nullspaces. Higher-order nondegeneracy conditions are needed to distinguish some geometrically different singularities sharing the same first-order ranks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A solution point is regular for natural-parameter continuation when \(\operatorname{rank}A=n\). It is parameter-singular when \(\operatorname{rank}A<n\). A parameter-singular point is an ordinary continuation fold candidate when
\[
\operatorname{rank}A=n-1,\qquad \operatorname{rank}B=n,
\]
so that the extended solution set remains a regular one-dimensional manifold although \(x\) is not locally a single-valued function of \(\lambda\). It is an extended singular point when \(\operatorname{rank}B<n\). A branch-point candidate is an extended singular point for which \(\dim\ker B\ge2\), indicating more than one independent first-order solution direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy compares the state Jacobian \(A=D_xF\) with the extended Jacobian \(B=[D_xF\ F_\lambda]\). Full rank of \(A\) gives an ordinary natural-parameter point. Loss of one rank in \(A\) while \(B\) remains full row rank is the first-order signature of a fold: the full solution curve is regular, but the physical parameter ceases to be a valid local coordinate. Rank loss in \(B\), especially a tangent nullspace of dimension at least two, marks a more singular configuration and a branch-point candidate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: At a fold candidate, \(\dim\ker B=1\), and every nonzero tangent \((\dot x,\dot\lambda)\in\ker B\) has \(\dot\lambda=0\).
Extended regularity is equivalent to \(B\) being surjective as a map from \(\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) to \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
special_cases_latex: For \(n=1\), a fold candidate satisfies \(F_x(x_*,\lambda_*)=0\) and \(F_\lambda(x_*,\lambda_*)\ne0\); a nondegenerate turning point additionally requires a suitable second derivative condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: Natural-parameter continuation can fail at a fold candidate even though an arclength parameterization remains locally admissible.
boundary_notes: Rank conditions identify candidates, not a complete bifurcation type; transcritical, pitchfork, cusp, and higher-codimension distinctions require higher derivatives and problem-specific nondegeneracy conditions.
No inspected local source supplied this exact taxonomy, so independent continuation literature is required.

notation.meaning: Jacobian with respect to state variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian-Based Taxonomy of Continuation Singularities
Fold-Point Continuation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Detect a simple fold through null-vector and transversality conditions, then cross it with pseudo-arclength continuation as the physical parameter reverses direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F:\mathbb{R}^n	imes\mathbb{R}	o\mathbb{R}^n\), a solution \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) is a simple fold when \(\operatorname{rank}F_x=n-1\), normalized vectors \(v,w\) satisfy \(F_xv=0\) and \(w^{\mathsf T}F_x=0\), and \[w^{\mathsf T}F_\lambda
eq0,\qquad w^{\mathsf T}F_{xx}[v,v]
eq0.\] Natural-parameter continuation must be replaced near this point by pseudo-arclength prediction and correction in the combined variable \((x,\lambda)\). A fold may be located by augmenting \(F(x,\lambda)=0\) with \(F_x(x,\lambda)v=0\) and a normalization equation \(c^{\mathsf T}v=1\), where \(c^{\mathsf T}v
eq0\). The pseudo-arclength path then crosses the fold while the parameter reverses direction.
assumptions_latex: The state Jacobian has one-dimensional right and left nullspaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pseudo-arclength continuation remains locally regular and traverses the fold although \(\lambda\) is not a valid local path parameter.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection and traversal of a simple fold on a one-parameter nonlinear solution curve.

notation.meaning: normalized right null vector of the state Jacobian
normalized left null vector of the state Jacobian
fixed normalization vector for fold localization

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Point Continuation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a branch point the full residual Jacobian loses rank; projected second-order compatibility selects outgoing tangents for separate branch-switching runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_*=[F_x(x_*,\lambda_*)\;F_\lambda(x_*,\lambda_*)]\). A branch point candidate satisfies \(F(x_*,\lambda_*)=0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}A_*<n\); in the generic corank-one case, \(\dim\ker A_*=2\), so two independent tangent directions \(t_1,t_2\) are available before higher-order compatibility is imposed. Locate the singular point with an augmented system containing the residual, a null-vector equation, and a normalization constraint. Determine admissible outgoing tangents from the second-order equation \[A_*z''+F_{zz}(z_*)[t,t]=0,\qquad z=(x,\lambda),\] projected onto the left nullspace of \(A_*\). Initialize separate predictor–corrector runs with the distinct admissible tangents, orienting each predictor away from the incoming branch.
assumptions_latex: The augmented residual Jacobian has the generic rank defect required for a two-dimensional tangent nullspace.
The projected second-order tangent equation has isolated admissible directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Distinct admissible tangents initialize continuation on the locally incident solution branches.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch detection and switching at a singular point of a one-parameter residual system.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the residual with respect to state and parameter
candidate tangent in the kernel of the augmented Jacobian

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Point Classification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify regular points, simple folds, and branch candidates using state and augmented Jacobian ranks, with higher derivatives needed to resolve actual branch geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a solution \(F(x_*,\lambda_*)=0\), define \(J_*=F_x(x_*,\lambda_*)\) and \(A_*=[J_*\;F_\lambda(x_*,\lambda_*)]\). The point is regular for natural-parameter continuation when \(\operatorname{rank}J_*=n\). It is a simple fold when \(\operatorname{rank}J_*=n-1\), \(\operatorname{rank}A_*=n\), and normalized null vectors \(J_*v=0\), \(w^{\mathsf T}J_*=0\) satisfy \(w^{\mathsf T}F_{xx}(x_*,\lambda_*)[v,v]\neq0\). It is a branch-point candidate when \(\operatorname{rank}A_*<n\). Rank conditions alone do not determine the number or geometry of incident branches; that classification requires projected higher derivatives or an equivalent reduced bifurcation equation.
assumptions_latex: Null vectors are normalized but otherwise arbitrary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ranks of \(J_*\) and \(A_*\), supplemented by projected curvature, distinguish the stated local singularity classes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank and transversality classification for regular points, simple folds, and branch candidates.

notation.meaning: state Jacobian at the classified solution
Jacobian with respect to the combined state-parameter variable
right and left state-Jacobian null vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Homotopy Path Formulations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embed the target residual in a parameterized family beginning at an easy system, then track the regular zero curve from parameter zero to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G,F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), with a known solution \(G(x_0)=0\). A basic linear homotopy is \[H(x,t)=(1-t)G(x)+tF(x),\qquad 0\leq t\leq1.\] More generally, any \(C^1\) map \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(H(x,0)=G(x)\) and \(H(x,1)=F(x)\) defines the path equation \(H(x,t)=0\). At every regular path point, a tangent \((\dot{x},\dot{t})\) satisfies \[H_x(x,t)\dot{x}+H_t(x,t)\dot{t}=0.\] If the connected regular path through \((x_0,0)\) reaches \((x_*,1)\), then \(F(x_*)=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(H\in C^1\) on a neighborhood of the tracked path.
The tracked component reaches parameter value \(t=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(x_*,1)=F(x_*)=0\) at any endpoint of the tracked component with \(t=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-curve formulation connecting an easy start system to a target residual system.

notation.meaning: start residual system with a known root
homotopy joining the start and target systems

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generic regularity, root accumulation, and finite length of the linear homotopy path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinates are consistently written as (x,λ). The extract's isolated reference to (0,a) conflicts with its homotopy definition and later endpoint statement and is reviewed as (a,0).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n be twice continuously differentiable and H(x,\lambda)=\lambda r(x)+(1-\lambda)(x-a). For almost every a\in\mathbb{R}^n, there is a zero path emanating from (a,0) along which [H_x(x,\lambda)\;H_\lambda(x,\lambda)] has full row rank n. If this path is bounded for \lambda\in[0,1), then it has an accumulation point (\bar{x},1) satisfying r(\bar{x})=0. If, additionally, J(\bar{x}) is nonsingular, the zero path between (a,0) and (\bar{x},1) has finite arc length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable residual and almost every starting vector, the linear homotopy has a regular zero path from its known initial zero. If that path remains bounded before the parameter reaches one, it accumulates at a root of the original system. A nonsingular residual Jacobian at the endpoint additionally gives finite path length.
assumptions_latex: a\in\mathbb{R}^n\text{ outside a measure-zero exceptional set}
\text{For the endpoint conclusion, the selected zero path is bounded for }\lambda\in[0,1)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\Gamma\text{ from }(a,0)\text{ with }\operatorname{rank}[H_x\;H_\lambda]=n\text{ along }\Gamma;\quad \Gamma\text{ bounded for }0\le\lambda<1\Rightarrow\exists(\bar{x},1)\in\operatorname{acc}(\Gamma),\ r(\bar{x})=0;\quad \det J(\bar{x})\ne0\Rightarrow\operatorname{length}(\Gamma)<\infty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear homotopy endpoints and the turning-point limitation of monotone-parameter tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General nonlinear systems; the endpoint identities are unconditional, whereas successful continuation requires following a zero-path branch to parameter one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n and a\in\mathbb{R}^n, define H(x,\lambda)=\lambda r(x)+(1-\lambda)(x-a). Then H(x,0)=x-a has the known zero x=a, and H(x,1)=r(x). Hence any tracked zero-path endpoint (x,1) satisfies r(x)=0. A scheme that insists on monotonically increasing \lambda can lose the zero path at a turning point; path-following continuation must permit \lambda to decrease when the path reverses in the \lambda-coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear homotopy begins with the easily solved equation x−a=0 and becomes the original residual equation at parameter one. Reaching parameter one on its zero path yields a root. Simply increasing the parameter can fail at a turning point, so practical continuation follows the path even when the parameter temporarily decreases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H(a,0)=0,\qquad H(x,1)=r(x),\qquad H(x,1)=0\Rightarrow r(x)=0;\quad \text{monotone-}\lambda\text{ tracking can fail at a turning point.}

knowledge_statements.title: Continuation–Homotopy Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuation curve in the zero set of a homotopy is a homotopy path when it reaches parameter values zero and one. At regular points its tangent is the null direction of the full Jacobian, and the homotopy parameter can be used locally wherever the state Jacobian is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(s\mapsto(x(s),\lambda(s))\), \(s\in[s_0,s_1]\), be a differentiable curve satisfying \(H(x(s),\lambda(s))=0\), \(\lambda(s_0)=0\), and \(\lambda(s_1)=1\). This continuation curve is a homotopy zero path connecting \(x(s_0)\), a zero of \(H(\cdot,0)\), to \(x(s_1)\), a zero of \(H(\cdot,1)\). At every point where \(D_{(x,\lambda)}H\) has rank \(n\), its tangent satisfies \[D_xH(x,\lambda)\dot{x}+D_\lambda H(x,\lambda)\dot{\lambda}=0.\] The tangent direction is determined up to orientation and normalization. If \(D_xH(x,\lambda)\) is nonsingular and \(\lambda\) is used as a local parameter, then \(dx/d\lambda=-D_xH(x,\lambda)^{-1}D_\lambda H(x,\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The curve is a homotopy zero path between the endpoint systems, and at each regular point its tangent belongs to \(\ker D_{(x,\lambda)}H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between a one-parameter homotopy and continuation along a regular zero-set curve that reaches both endpoint parameter values.

notation.meaning: full Jacobian with respect to the state and homotopy parameter
