knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Diagnostic Agreement Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QR and SVD rank tests agree when both separate the same leading and trailing subspaces across a common tolerance; values near that tolerance make agreement uncertified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(AP=QR\) be a rank-revealing QR factorization partitioned at index \(r\), and let \(\sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_p\) be the singular values of \(A\). For a common tolerance \(\tau>0\), suppose \[\sigma_r>\tau\geq\sigma_{r+1},\qquad \sigma_{\min}(R_{11})>\tau,\qquad \|R_{22}\|_2\leq\tau.\] Then the SVD threshold count and the QR block test both report numerical rank \(r\). If either diagnostic has values within its perturbation or rounding uncertainty of \(\tau\), agreement is not certified and the rank decision must be treated as tolerance-sensitive.
assumptions_latex: The QR and SVD diagnostics use the same \(\tau>0\).
The displayed QR and singular-value separation inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both diagnostics return numerical rank \(r\); absent separation from \(\tau\), agreement is not certified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient separation conditions for QR- and SVD-based numerical-rank diagnostics to agree.

notation.meaning: Leading and trailing blocks of the rank-revealing QR factor.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The displayed exact inequalities make the agreement conclusion logically valid, but the cited sources do not explicitly support the combined QR–SVD agreement criterion. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectrally filtered regularized least-squares family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i)V^T\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(\alpha\ge0\) be a regularization parameter. A spectral filter is a family of scalar functions \(\varphi_\alpha:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear least squares with rank deficiency or ill conditioning; both truncated-SVD and Tikhonov/Levenberg regularization are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank-aware regularized solve family is \(x_\alpha=\sum_{\sigma_i>0}\varphi_\alpha(\sigma_i)(u_i^Tb)v_i\), where the filter suppresses directions with small \(\sigma_i\). The truncated-SVD member uses \(\varphi_\tau(\sigma)=\sigma^{-1}\mathbf1_{\{\sigma>\tau\}}\). The Tikhonov member uses \(\varphi_\lambda(\sigma)=\sigma/(\sigma^2+\lambda)\) for \(\lambda>0\), equivalently \(x_\lambda\) is the unique minimizer of \(\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_2^2\) and satisfies \((A^TA+\lambda I)x_\lambda=A^Tb\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-aware regularized solve applies a scalar filter to every singular component of the data. Truncated SVD removes components whose singular values do not exceed a threshold. Tikhonov regularization continuously damps every component, with the strongest damping in small-singular-value directions, and is equivalently the unique minimizer of a least-squares objective plus a positive quadratic penalty.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x_\lambda=\arg\min_x\left(\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_2^2\right)\) for \(\lambda>0\).
The Tikhonov system is the normal equation of \(\min_x\left\|\begin{bmatrix}A\\\sqrt\lambda I\end{bmatrix}x-\begin{bmatrix}b\\0\end{bmatrix}\right\|_2^2\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\tau=0\), truncated SVD yields \(A^\dagger b\).
If \(A\) has full column rank, then \(x_\lambda\to(A^TA)^{-1}A^Tb\) as \(\lambda\downarrow0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), \(A^TA+\lambda I\) is positive definite even when \(A\) is rank deficient.
Both filters reduce amplification by reciprocals of small singular values.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a parameter-choice rule.
General penalties \(\|Lx\|_2^2\) require a generalized spectral decomposition and are outside this slot.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Solves
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard singular directions at or below the threshold and solve only in the retained singular subspace, returning zero if no direction is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(q=\min\{m,n\}\) and let \(A=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^{q}\sigma_i u_i v_i^{\mathsf T}\) be a compact singular value decomposition, where \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\), \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), and \(\sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_q\geq0\). Given \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\tau>0\), define \(I_\tau=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}:\sigma_i>\tau\}\) and \(A_\tau=\sum_{i\in I_\tau}\sigma_i u_i v_i^{\mathsf T}\). The truncated solve returns
\[
p_\tau=-\sum_{i\in I_\tau}\frac{u_i^{\mathsf T}b}{\sigma_i}v_i=-A_\tau^\dagger b.
\]
No singular component at or below \(\tau\) is retained; if \(I_\tau=\varnothing\), the output is \(p_\tau=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(A=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) is a compact singular value decomposition with \(q=\min\{m,n\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_\tau=-A_\tau^\dagger b\) using exactly the singular values satisfying \(\sigma_i>\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated-SVD solution of a possibly rank-deficient linearized residual equation.

notation.meaning: smaller of the row and column dimensions of A
rank-truncated approximation of the linearized operator
Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the truncated operator

knowledge_statements.title: Damped Solves
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive quadratic penalty to least squares, yielding a unique damped step even when the linearized operator is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\lambda>0\), define
\[
p_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\bigl(\lVert Ap+b\rVert_2^2+\lambda^2\lVert p\rVert_2^2\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, compute \(p_\lambda\) from
\[
(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda^2I_n)p_\lambda=-A^{\mathsf T}b,
\]
where \(I_n\) is the \(n\times n\) identity matrix. Because \(\lambda>0\), the coefficient matrix is positive definite and the output \(p_\lambda\) is the unique minimizer. An iterative implementation may stop when its normal-equation residual satisfies a prescribed linear-solve tolerance.

notation.meaning: identity matrix on the step space

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Norm Solves
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pseudoinverse returns the unique least-squares solution having smallest Euclidean norm; for a consistent system it is orthogonal to the null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), the minimum-norm least-squares step is
\[
p_*=-A^\dagger b.
\]
It is the unique vector satisfying
\[
p_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\lVert Ap+b\rVert_2,
\qquad
\lVert p_*\rVert_2=\min\{\lVert p\rVert_2:p\text{ minimizes }\lVert Ap+b\rVert_2\}.
\]
If \(Ap=-b\) is consistent, this reduces to the unique solution orthogonal to \(\ker A\). If \(A\) has full row rank, \(p_*=-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_*=-A^\dagger b\) uniquely minimizes residual norm and then solution norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Aware Solve Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate numerical rank, use an ordinary solve when well conditioned, and otherwise choose truncation, minimum norm, or damping according to null-direction policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), rank threshold \(\tau>0\), and damping \(\lambda>0\), estimate singular values \(\sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_q\). Set \(r_\tau=|\{i:\sigma_i>\tau\}|\). If \(r_\tau=q\) and the estimated condition ratio \(\sigma_1/\sigma_q\) is acceptable, solve \(Ap=-b\) or its least-squares form without regularization. If numerical rank deficiency is intentional, return the truncated or minimum-norm step. If discarded directions must remain continuously controlled, return the damped step. Terminate after the selected linear solver meets its residual tolerance and report \(r_\tau\), the method, and its regularization parameter.
assumptions_latex: A condition-number acceptance threshold and null-direction policy are supplied
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a linearized step together with its estimated numerical rank and regularization metadata.

notation.meaning: number of singular values, equal to the smaller matrix dimension

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaling and preconditioning interface for a linearized residual system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable, let \(J=F'(x)\), and consider the linearized least-squares problem \(\min_p\|Jp+F(x)\|_2\). Let \(D_x\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(D_F\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be positive diagonal matrices, and let \(P\) be a nonsingular preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional large-scale residual systems; matrices may be represented by operator actions rather than explicitly stored arrays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scaling-preconditioning interface is the transformed operator and right-hand side \(\mathcal A=P^{-1}D_FJD_x^{-1}\) and \(c=-P^{-1}D_FF(x)\), together with the recovery map \(p=D_x^{-1}z\), where the iterative linear solver approximately minimizes \(\|\mathcal Az-c\|_2\). Variable scaling is encoded by \(D_x\), residual scaling by \(D_F\), and left preconditioning by the application of \(P^{-1}\). The interface is matrix-free when it supplies only the actions of \(J\), \(J^T\), \(P^{-1}\), and their required transposes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface transforms the linearized residual problem by scaling variables and residual components and by applying an invertible left preconditioner. The iterative solver works in the scaled variable, while the physical step is recovered with the inverse variable scaling. In a matrix-free realization, only operator actions and their required transpose actions are exposed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(P=I\), the interface is the weighted least-squares problem \(\min_p\|D_F(Jp+F(x))\|_2\) expressed in coordinates \(z=D_xp\).
If \(D_x=D_F=I\), only the preconditioned linearized operator remains.
special_cases_latex: Typical-magnitude scaling uses \((D_x)_{ii}=1/\operatorname{typ}x_i\) and \((D_F)_{jj}=1/\operatorname{typ}F_j\).
Right preconditioning can be represented by absorbing an additional nonsingular factor into the recovery map.
immediate_consequences_latex: The scaled step norm is \(\|D_xp\|_2=\|z\|_2\).
Residual components are compared in the common units induced by \(D_F\).
boundary_notes: A nonsymmetric left preconditioner changes the minimized norm; this must be intentional.
The definition does not guarantee improved convergence for an arbitrary preconditioner.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Typical-magnitude variable and residual scaling
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\). For each variable and residual component, choose positive typical magnitudes \(s_i^x>0\) and \(s_j^F>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal scaling for nonlinear equations and residual-based optimization in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The variable-residual scaling pair associated with the typical magnitudes is \(D_x=\operatorname{diag}((s_1^x)^{-1},\ldots,(s_n^x)^{-1})\) and \(D_F=\operatorname{diag}((s_1^F)^{-1},\ldots,(s_m^F)^{-1})\). The scaled variable, residual, step, and Jacobian are \(\widehat x=D_xx\), \(\widehat F(x)=D_FF(x)\), \(\widehat p=D_xp\), and \(\widehat J=D_FJ(x)D_x^{-1}\). A pair is balanced at a reference region when typical components of \(\widehat x\) and of \(\widehat F\) away from a root have magnitudes of order one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose positive typical magnitudes for every variable and residual component. Their reciprocals form two diagonal matrices. These matrices nondimensionalize variables, steps, residuals, and the Jacobian. The pair is balanced when components that are typical for the application become comparable in magnitude after scaling.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The scaled linearized residual is \(D_F(F(x)+Jp)=\widehat F(x)+\widehat J\widehat p\).
The scale-aware step norm is \(\|D_xp\|_2\), and the scale-aware residual norm is \(\|D_FF(x)\|_2\) or \(\|D_FF(x)\|_\infty\).
special_cases_latex: If no scaling is required, all typical magnitudes equal one and \(D_x=D_F=I\).
Unit conversion is represented by a corresponding change of positive diagonal entries.
immediate_consequences_latex: Residual components with different physical units contribute comparably after appropriate scaling.
The transformed Jacobian records both row and column scaling.
boundary_notes: Typical magnitudes must be strictly positive even when a component's current value is zero.
Dynamic rescaling is a nearby variant and is not part of the fixed pair.

notation.meaning: typical magnitude of variable component i
typical magnitude of residual component j

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Scaling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive diagonal variable transformation scales Jacobian columns and maps each scaled step to a unique physical step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable, let \(x_c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(D_x\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be diagonal with strictly positive entries. Introduce \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) by
\[
x=x_c+D_xz,
\qquad
\widehat F(z)=F(x_c+D_xz).
\]
Then
\[
J_{\widehat F}(z)=J_F(x_c+D_xz)D_x.
\]
Consequently, if \(x=x_c+D_xz\) and \(s_z\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(J_F(x)D_xs_z=-F(x)\), the corresponding physical correction is \(s_x=D_xs_z\). Since \(D_x\) is nonsingular, scaled and unscaled variables correspond one-to-one.
assumptions_latex: \(D_x\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal change of variables for a nonlinear residual equation.

notation.meaning: reference point for the scaled coordinates

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Scaling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal residual scaling weights equations and Jacobian rows while leaving the nonlinear system’s zero set unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable and let \(D_r\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be diagonal with strictly positive entries. Define the scaled residual
\[
\widetilde F(x)=D_rF(x).
\]
Its Jacobian satisfies
\[
J_{\widetilde F}(x)=D_rJ_F(x).
\]
Because \(D_r\) is nonsingular, \(\widetilde F(x)=0\) if and only if \(F(x)=0\). Thus residual scaling preserves the solution set while weighting the equations in residual norms and left-scaling every linearized system.
assumptions_latex: \(D_r\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal row scaling of residuals and their linearization.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Compatibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The variable and residual scalings are compatible when the Jacobian is transformed on both sides and scaled steps are mapped back with the variable-scaling matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable, let \(x_c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(D_x\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(D_r\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular diagonal matrices with positive entries. Define \(x=x_c+D_xz\) and \(G(z)=D_rF(x_c+D_xz)\). Variable and residual scaling are algebraically compatible with the linearization when the implemented scaled Jacobian and step recovery satisfy
\[
J_G(z)=D_rJ_F(x_c+D_xz)D_x,
\qquad
s_x=D_xs_z.
\]
Under these identities, the scaled linear model is the image of the unscaled linear model under the residual and variable coordinate transformations.
assumptions_latex: \(D_x\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(D_r\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) are nonsingular positive diagonal matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chain-rule consistency required between variable scaling, residual scaling, and step recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized-System Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular left and right preconditioners preserve the physical solution while transforming the operator seen by an iterative linear solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(Jp=-r\), where \(J\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and let \(M_L,M_R\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular preconditioners. Left preconditioning gives
\[
M_L^{-1}Jp=-M_L^{-1}r.
\]
Right preconditioning substitutes \(p=M_R^{-1}y\) and gives
\[
JM_R^{-1}y=-r,
\qquad p=M_R^{-1}y.
\]
Split preconditioning combines both transformations as \(M_L^{-1}JM_R^{-1}y=-M_L^{-1}r\). In exact arithmetic all three systems have the same physical solution \(p\); their purpose is to produce a transformed operator more favorable for an iterative linear solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Left, right, and split preconditioned systems recover the same solution \(p=-J^{-1}r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent left, right, and split preconditioned forms of a nonsingular linearized system.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The left, right, and split transformations are standard and internally correct, and representation is suitable for the topic. However, the record has no citation, so its preconditioning conventions and scope cannot enter candidate-review knowledge without an authoritative source and specific locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioner for a linearized residual equation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a nonsingular linearized-system matrix and consider \(Ap=b\). Let \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and inexpensive to solve with relative to \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic Krylov solution of square linearized systems; rectangular least-squares analogues use corresponding left and right operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A left preconditioner for \(Ap=b\) is a nonsingular matrix \(M\) for which the transformed system \(M^{-1}Ap=M^{-1}b\) is supplied to the iterative solver. A right preconditioner uses \(AM^{-1}z=b\) and recovers \(p=M^{-1}z\). For symmetric positive-definite \(A\), an SPD preconditioner \(M=C C^T\) induces the symmetrically preconditioned operator \(C^{-1}AC^{-T}\). The preconditioner is spectrally effective when the eigenvalues or singular values of the transformed operator are more tightly clustered than those of the original operator, while applications of \(M^{-1}\) remain computationally inexpensive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearized system is preconditioned by transforming it with an invertible approximation that is cheap to solve. Left preconditioning transforms both operator and right-hand side. Right preconditioning changes variables and recovers the physical step afterward. In the symmetric positive-definite case, symmetric preconditioning preserves the structure needed by conjugate gradients. Effectiveness means improving the transformed spectrum at acceptable application cost.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For SPD \(A\) and \(M=CC^T\), solve \(C^{-1}AC^{-T}y=C^{-1}b\) and set \(p=C^{-T}y\).
An ideal preconditioner satisfies \(M^{-1}A\approx I\), subject to the cost of applying \(M^{-1}\).
special_cases_latex: Diagonal preconditioning takes \(M=\operatorname{diag}(A)\) when its diagonal is suitable.
Incomplete Cholesky uses \(M=\widetilde L\widetilde L^T\) with a sparse approximate factor \(\widetilde L\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact solutions are unchanged by nonsingular left or right preconditioning after the stated recovery map.
Krylov convergence is governed by the transformed rather than the original operator.
boundary_notes: Nonsingular preconditioning does not repair inconsistency of a square equation.
Indefinite and nonsymmetric systems require Krylov methods compatible with their transformed structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structure-informed block preconditioner family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a linearized multiphysics system be partitioned as \(A=[A_{ij}]_{i,j=1}^s\) according to physical fields, with unknown \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_s)\). Assume selected diagonal blocks or Schur complements admit inexpensive approximate solves.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional block systems arising from coupled physical models; the definition covers block diagonal and block triangular approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A physics-informed block preconditioner is a nonsingular block matrix \(M\) whose partition matches the physical-field partition of \(A\), and whose blocks approximate field operators or coupling Schur complements. The block-Jacobi member is \(M_D=\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde A_{11},\ldots,\widetilde A_{ss})\). For a two-field system \(A=\begin{bmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{bmatrix}\), a block-triangular member is \(M_T=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde A_{11}&A_{12}\\0&\widetilde S\end{bmatrix}\), where \(\widetilde S\) approximates \(S=A_{22}-A_{21}A_{11}^{-1}A_{12}\). Membership requires that applications of each approximate inverse be defined and cheaper than solving the full coupled system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A physics-informed block preconditioner respects the partition of the unknowns into physical fields. Its component solves approximate individual field operators, while triangular variants also approximate the Schur complement describing inter-field coupling. The family includes block-diagonal and block-triangular forms, provided their component inverse actions are well defined and less expensive than solving the full system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_D=\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde A_{ii}),\qquad M_T=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde A_{11}&A_{12}\\0&\widetilde S\end{bmatrix},\quad \widetilde S\approx A_{22}-A_{21}A_{11}^{-1}A_{12}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: A block-diagonal preconditioner neglects inter-field coupling in its inverse application.
A block-triangular preconditioner retains one coupling direction and represents the remaining coupling through a Schur-complement approximation.
special_cases_latex: For uncoupled fields, \(A_{ij}=0\) for \(i\ne j\), and exact diagonal blocks give \(M_D=A\).
A coarse-grid PDE solve may serve as an approximate inverse for a field block.
immediate_consequences_latex: The block partition determines which physical subsolvers can be reused.
With exact two-by-two block factors, the corresponding block factorization reproduces the full system.
boundary_notes: Physical plausibility alone does not guarantee spectral effectiveness.
Singular diagonal blocks require alternative factorizations or constraint-aware preconditioners.

knowledge_statements.title: Physics-Based Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate the Jacobian with a cheaply invertible operator retaining dominant physical couplings, and assess it through the preconditioned defect.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a discretized nonlinear model have Jacobian decomposition \(J=J_{\mathrm{dom}}+J_{\mathrm{rem}}\), where \(J_{\mathrm{dom}}\) represents dominant couplings identified by the governing model. A physics-based preconditioner chooses an efficiently invertible \(M\approx J_{\mathrm{dom}}\) and applies \(M^{-1}\) without requiring exact inversion of \(J\). The construction is admissible when \(M\) is nonsingular on the solver space and its application is cheaper than solving with \(J\). Its algebraic quality is measured by the preconditioned defect
\[
I-M^{-1}J=-M^{-1}(J-M).
\]
A small or spectrally favorable defect indicates that the retained physical approximation captures the difficult modes of the linearized system.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is nonsingular and can be applied efficiently
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I-M^{-1}J=-M^{-1}(J-M)\) quantifies the neglected modeled couplings after preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioner formed from a tractable approximation retaining dominant modeled physics.

notation.meaning: Jacobian contribution from dominant modeled physics

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Principle is the correct role, but the model-dependent notion of dominant physics and the claim that a favorable defect captures difficult modes require authoritative support. No source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exploit a field partition by approximately solving a principal block and its Schur complement in a block-triangular preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a two-field linearized system
\[
J=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix},
\]
assume \(A\) is nonsingular and define the Schur complement \(S=D-CA^{-1}B\). The exact block factorization is
\[
J=\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\ CA^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\0&S\end{pmatrix}.
\]
A block preconditioner replaces \(A\) and \(S\) by efficiently invertible approximations \(\widehat A\) and \(\widehat S\), for example
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat A&B\\0&\widehat S\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Applying \(M^{-1}\) consists of successive approximate block solves and preserves the partition of the coupled unknowns.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) has a conforming two-by-two block partition
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The block-triangular \(M\) approximates the exact factorization governed by \(S=D-CA^{-1}B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-triangular preconditioning through an approximate Schur complement.

knowledge_statements.title: Physics-Informed Block Structure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition variables and residuals by physical fields so diagonal blocks represent subsystem responses and off-diagonal blocks represent modeled couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the state be partitioned by modeled fields as \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\), and partition the residual compatibly as \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_k)\). The Jacobian then has block representation
\[
J_F(x)=\bigl[J_{ij}(x)\bigr]_{i,j=1}^k,
\qquad
J_{ij}(x)=\frac{\partial F_i}{\partial x_j}(x).
\]
A zero block \(J_{ij}=0\) records absence of direct linearized influence of field \(x_j\) on residual subsystem \(F_i\); a nonzero off-diagonal block records a modeled coupling. A physics-informed block structure preserves this field-to-subsystem correspondence when constructing block factorizations or preconditioners.
assumptions_latex: Variable and residual partitions are conforming
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_F=[J_{ij}]\) with \(J_{ij}=\partial F_i/\partial x_j\), so block sparsity encodes direct linearized coupling.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Field partition mapping modeled subsystems and couplings to Jacobian blocks.

notation.meaning: variables belonging to modeled field j

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_n\in\mathbb R^{m_n\times n}\) be a family of linearized-system matrices with dimensions tending to infinity. Let \(N_n=m_nn\) and let \(\operatorname{nnz}(A_n)\) count stored nonzeros.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic finite-dimensional matrix families; classes may overlap and describe exploitable representation rather than numerical conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A large-scale system family is sparse when \(\operatorname{nnz}(A_n)=o(N_n)\); banded with bandwidth \(w_n\) when \((A_n)_{ij}=0\) for \(|i-j|>w_n\); block structured when fixed partitions expose submatrices \((A_n)_{ij}\) admitting block operations; matrix-free when algorithms access \(A_nv\) and, when needed, \(A_n^Tu\) without storing all entries; and partially separable or assembled when \(A_n=\sum_{\ell=1}^{q_n}E_\ell^TA_{n,\ell}R_\ell\) with local operators of uniformly bounded or controlled dimension. The structure signature is the subset of these properties possessed by the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family of growing linearized systems is classified by its exploitable representation. It may have asymptotically few nonzeros, bounded or slowly growing bandwidth, a meaningful block partition, only operator access, or an assembly from local operators. These classes are not mutually exclusive; their collection forms the structure signature used to select storage, factorization, Krylov, and preconditioning strategies.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Matrix-free representation means that the action oracle replaces explicit entry storage in the selected algorithm.
Bandedness is a special sparsity pattern; block structure concerns a partition and need not imply sparsity inside blocks.
special_cases_latex: A PDE discretization can be simultaneously sparse, assembled, block structured, and matrix-free.
A dense low-dimensional matrix has an empty large-scale structure signature under this definition.
immediate_consequences_latex: Direct sparse factorization additionally depends on fill under ordering, not solely on \(\operatorname{nnz}(A_n)\).
Krylov methods can operate on matrix-free families when the required operator and transpose actions are available.
boundary_notes: Low rank, hierarchical matrices, and tensor formats are nearby structure classes not included here.
Large dimension alone is not a structural property.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free system exposes Jacobian-vector products, computed by directional differentiation or approximated by small finite differences, without assembling or storing the Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable at \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), with Jacobian \(J(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). A linearized system involving \(J(x)\) is matrix-free when the solver does not assemble or store the entries of \(J(x)\) and instead accesses the operator through products \(v\mapsto J(x)v\) for \(v\in\mathbb R^n\). The exact Jacobian-vector product is
\[
J(x)v=\left.\frac{d}{dt}F(x+tv)\right|_{t=0}.
\]
If exact directional differentiation is unavailable, then for fixed \(v\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
J(x)v=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{F(x+hv)-F(x)}{h},
\]
so a sufficiently small nonzero \(h\) yields a forward-difference approximation. A compatible iterative solver uses operator products, residual vectors, and optional preconditioner applications without requiring individual Jacobian entries.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is differentiable at \(x\in\mathbb R^n\)
The iterative linear solver can operate using matrix-vector products
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linearized operator is represented by the action \(v\mapsto J(x)v\), not by stored matrix entries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized systems accessed through operator products rather than an assembled matrix.

notation.meaning: Jacobian-vector product at the current nonlinear iterate
nonzero directional-difference increment tending to zero in the defining limit

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.1 Structure and Sparsity p. 56

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning variables and residuals gives the Jacobian and linearized root equation a block structure. In the square solvable case, the block equations define the ordinary Newton correction, while structural zero blocks can support sparse storage and preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^{n_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb{R}^{n_p}\to\mathbb{R}^{m_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb{R}^{m_q}\) be differentiable on a domain \(\mathcal D\), with \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\) and \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_q)\). Its Jacobian has the block representation \[J_F(x)=\bigl[J_{ij}(x)\bigr]_{i=1,j=1}^{q,p},\qquad J_{ij}(x)=\frac{\partial F_i(x)}{\partial x_j}\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i\times n_j}.\] Accordingly, the linearized root equation \(J_F(x)s=-F(x)\), whenever it is imposed, is equivalent to \[\sum_{j=1}^{p}J_{ij}(x)s_j=-F_i(x),\qquad i=1,\ldots,q.\] When \(\sum_{j=1}^{p}n_j=\sum_{i=1}^{q}m_i\) and this linear system is solvable, its solution is the ordinary Newton correction. A declared structural zero block means \(J_{ij}(x)=0\) for every \(x\in\mathcal D\), permitting block-sparse storage and block preconditioning.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable on the modeled domain \(\mathcal D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Jacobian is represented by blocks \(J_{ij}(x)\), and the linearized root equation decomposes into the displayed coupled block equations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block representation of a differentiable nonlinear residual system and its linearized root equation.

notation.meaning: Jacobian block coupling residual block i to variable block j.
Modeled domain of the residual mapping.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.2 Structured Systems p. 57

knowledge_statements.title: Partitioned Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partitioned system divides variable and residual indices into disjoint blocks and may record which variable blocks each residual block depends upon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A residual system \(F(x)=0\), with \(F:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\), is partitioned when index families \(\{I_j\}_{j=1}^{p}\) and \(\{K_i\}_{i=1}^{q}\) are disjoint partitions of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), respectively. Writing \(x_j=x_{I_j}\) and \(F_i(x)=F(x)_{K_i}\) yields \[x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p),\qquad F(x)=(F_1(x),\ldots,F_q(x)).\] The partition is dependency-aware when each \(F_i\) is supplied with a set \(D_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) such that \(F_i\) depends only on \(\{x_j:j\in D_i\}\).
assumptions_latex: The index families are nonempty disjoint covers of their respective index sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system admits compatible variable and residual block decompositions, optionally augmented by dependency sets \(D_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partitioned residual systems with compatible variable and equation decompositions.

notation.meaning: Variable blocks on which residual block i depends.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.2 Structured Systems p. 57

knowledge_statements.title: Large-Scale Structure Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose explicit blocks, partitioned evaluation, or matrix-free products according to available operations, and keep scaling and preconditioning compatible with that representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=0\), select the representation that preserves every reliably available operation needed by the solver while minimizing unavailable or unnecessarily expensive ones. Use explicit block storage when Jacobian blocks \(J_{ij}(x)\) are formable and reusable; use a partitioned interface when residual blocks and their dependencies can be evaluated separately; and use a matrix-free interface when products \(J_F(x)v\) or \(J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}w\) are available without forming \(J_F(x)\). Any preconditioner \(M_k\) must act on the same scaled linearization and respect the selected variable-residual partition.
assumptions_latex: A residual evaluation interface and at least one usable derivative operation are available.
The solver's required linear-algebra operations are known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected representation exposes usable structure without requiring derivative operations that the implementation cannot provide.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule for exposing structure to a large-scale residual solver.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The principle combines explicit blocks, partitioned evaluation, matrix-free products, scaling, and preconditioner compatibility. The sole structured-systems locator does not provide inspectable support for all of these implementation-selection requirements, so the exact policy cannot be validated from the supplied evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite nonlinear-solver diagnostic state
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an iterative solver generate \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\) for either \(F(x)=0\) or \(\min f(x)\). Let \(D_x,D_F\) be positive diagonal scalings and let positive tolerances and finite resource limits be specified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision, deterministic nonlinear equations and unconstrained minimization; the system separates successful convergence from stagnation and resource failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver stopping-testing diagnostic system is a tuple \(\mathcal D_k=(r_k,g_k,s_k,a_k,q_k)\), where for nonlinear equations \(r_k=\|D_FF(x_k)\|_\infty\), for minimization \(g_k\) is a scale-aware gradient measure, \(s_k=\max_i |(x_k-x_{k-1})_i|/\max\{|(x_k)_i|,\operatorname{typ}x_i\}\), \(a_k\) is an actual-to-predicted model-reduction ratio when a model step is used, and \(q_k\) records iteration, evaluation, or step-length limits. A termination label is successful only when the problem-specific residual or stationarity test holds; small \(s_k\) alone labels stagnation unless accompanied by success.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The diagnostic system records a scaled residual or stationarity measure, relative step size, model-agreement information, and resource-limit state. Successful termination requires the appropriate solution test. A small step without a sufficiently small residual or stationarity measure is classified as stagnation rather than convergence. Exhausted iteration or evaluation limits receive a separate resource label.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For root finding, \(r_k\) may be replaced by a componentwise condition \(|F_i(x_k)|\le\varepsilon_F\operatorname{typ}F_i\) for every \(i\).
Relative step stopping is the infinity norm of the componentwise scaled displacement.
special_cases_latex: At the initial point, the step diagnostic is omitted and the success tests are applied directly.
For a pure line-search method without a trust-region model, \(a_k\) may be absent.
immediate_consequences_latex: The label distinguishes convergence to a root from convergence to a nonroot stationary point of a residual merit function.
Scaling prevents a single large-unit component from dominating every test.
boundary_notes: Passing a stopping test is a numerical certificate at stated tolerances, not an exact-solution assertion.
Stochastic and noisy stopping systems require statistical modifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Residual Stopping Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop for a root only when the scaled residual meets absolute-plus-relative tolerance; this alone does not certify a nearby exact root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\), a candidate \(x_k\) passes the root-residual diagnostic when \[\|D_FF(x_k)\|\le \tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\|D_FF(x_0)\|,\] where \(D_F\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is a fixed nonsingular residual scaling and \(\tau_{\mathrm{abs}},\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\). The diagnostic certifies only that \(x_k\) is an approximate zero at the declared scaled tolerance. It does not certify nonsingularity of \(J_F(x_k)\), proximity to an exact root, or successful least-squares stationarity when the residual cannot vanish.
assumptions_latex: The norm and nonsingular residual scaling \(D_F\) are fixed for the test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality certifies scaled residual termination, but no stronger local-solution property.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled residual certificate for approximate roots of square or nonsquare systems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled root-residual stopping test
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(x_k\) be a candidate root, and choose positive typical residual magnitudes \(s_i^F\). Set \(D_F=\operatorname{diag}(1/s_i^F)\) and choose \(\varepsilon_F>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional root finding with componentwise residual scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The scaled root-residual diagnostic is \(R_F(x_k)=\|D_FF(x_k)\|_\infty=\max_i |F_i(x_k)|/s_i^F\). The root-residual stopping condition is \(R_F(x_k)\le\varepsilon_F\), equivalently \(|F_i(x_k)|\le\varepsilon_Fs_i^F\) for every component \(i\). A relative reduction diagnostic may additionally be recorded as \(R_F(x_k)/\max\{R_F(x_0),1\}\), but it does not replace the absolute scaled test unless a separate acceptance contract says so.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale every residual component by a positive typical magnitude and take the largest scaled magnitude. The candidate passes the root-residual test exactly when every residual component lies within its scaled tolerance. Relative reduction from the starting residual can be reported as supplementary information, but the primary condition is the componentwise scaled residual bound.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\|D_FF(x_k)\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_F\iff |F_i(x_k)|\le\varepsilon_Fs_i^F\) for all \(i\).
special_cases_latex: If all residual components share a common scale \(s\), then the test is \(\|F(x_k)\|_\infty\le s\varepsilon_F\).
With \(D_F=I\), the diagnostic becomes the unscaled infinity norm.
immediate_consequences_latex: No residual component can be hidden by cancellation with another component.
Changing physical units together with the corresponding typical magnitudes leaves the dimensionless diagnostic unchanged.
boundary_notes: A small residual does not by itself bound distance to a root without regularity or error-bound assumptions.
For inconsistent overdetermined equations, stationarity of a least-squares merit function may be the relevant alternative test.

notation.meaning: positive typical magnitude of residual component i

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Stationarity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonlinear least squares, test the scaled gradient J-transpose times residual; a small value certifies stationarity, not a root or minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\) for differentiable \(F:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\). Since \(\nabla\phi(x)=J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}F(x)\), a candidate \(x_k\) passes the scaled stationarity diagnostic when \[\|D_x^{-1}J_F(x_k)^{\mathsf T}F(x_k)\|_{\infty}\le \tau_g,\] where \(D_x\) is nonsingular variable scaling and \(\tau_g\ge0\). This certifies approximate first-order stationarity of the least-squares objective at the declared tolerance, not that \(F(x_k)=0\), nor that \(x_k\) is a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality certifies approximate first-order stationarity of \(\phi\), but not residual vanishing or local minimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order stationarity certificate for unconstrained nonlinear least squares.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled stationarity test for nonlinear least squares
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable with Jacobian \(J(x)\), and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2\). Choose positive variable scales \(s_i^x\), a positive objective scale \(s_f\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon_g>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional unconstrained nonlinear least squares; the test diagnoses first-order stationarity, not necessarily a root or local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Since \(\nabla f(x)=J(x)^Tr(x)\), define the scale-aware stationarity diagnostic \(G(x)=\max_i |(J(x)^Tr(x))_i|\max\{|x_i|,s_i^x\}/\max\{|f(x)|,s_f\}\). A candidate \(x_k\) is declared approximately stationary when \(G(x_k)\le\varepsilon_g\). The accompanying root diagnostic \(\|D_Fr(x_k)\|_\infty\) must be reported separately: stationarity with a non-small residual describes a stationary point of the least-squares objective rather than a solved residual equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonlinear least-squares objective, the gradient is the transpose Jacobian times the residual. Scale each gradient component by a typical variable magnitude and normalize by a typical objective magnitude. The largest normalized component is the stationarity diagnostic. Passing this test means approximate first-order stationarity, but it does not imply that the residual is small, so the root-residual diagnostic remains separate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Unscaled first-order stationarity is \(J(x)^Tr(x)=0\).
For linear least squares \(r(x)=Ax-b\), stationarity is the normal equation \(A^T(Ax-b)=0\).
special_cases_latex: At an exact root \(r(x)=0\), the stationarity diagnostic is zero.
If \(r\) is affine, every stationary point is a global least-squares minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: A nonroot stationary point satisfies \(J(x)^Tr(x)\approx0\) while \(r(x)\) remains non-small.
The diagnostic is dimensionless when the supplied scales carry the corresponding units.
boundary_notes: First-order stationarity does not distinguish minima, maxima, and saddle points in nonlinear least squares.
Near-zero objective values require the positive floor \(s_f\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative-step and model-agreement diagnostics
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(m_k\) be a local model at \(x_k\) with \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\), and let \(p_k\) be a trial step with positive predicted reduction \(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)>0\). Choose positive typical variable magnitudes \(s_i^x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic line-search or trust-region iterations with an explicit local model and finite-dimensional variable scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The step-model agreement diagnostic pair is \((S_k,\rho_k)\), where \(S_k=\max_i |(p_k)_i|/\max\{|(x_k+p_k)_i|,s_i^x\}\) is the maximum relative componentwise step and \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)]/[m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)]\) is the ratio of actual to predicted reduction. Small \(S_k\) diagnoses negligible movement at the chosen scale; \(\rho_k\) near one diagnoses accurate prediction over the trial step; \(\rho_k<0\) records an objective increase despite positive predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pair combines a scale-aware measure of how far the iterate moved with the ratio between actual and model-predicted reduction. A tiny relative step signals stagnation or convergence but does not identify which. A ratio near one indicates good model agreement, while a negative ratio means the objective increased even though the model predicted improvement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The numerator of \(\rho_k\) is actual reduction and its denominator is predicted reduction.
If \(p_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), then \(S_k\) is the infinity norm of the componentwise relative iterate change.
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic objective with its exact quadratic model, \(\rho_k=1\) whenever the denominator is positive.
If \(p_k=0\), then \(S_k=0\), while \(\rho_k\) is undefined because predicted reduction is zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: Step acceptance and trust-radius updates can be conditioned on \(\rho_k\).
A small-step failure can be distinguished from a poor-model failure by examining both components.
boundary_notes: The ratio is undefined when predicted reduction is zero or negative.
Good agreement does not itself imply stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Step Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled accepted step below tolerance is diagnostically small, but does not alone establish a root, stationarity, or successful convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an accepted step \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), define the scaled relative step measure \[\sigma_k=\frac{\|D_xs_k\|}{1+\|D_xx_k\|},\] where \(D_x\) is fixed and nonsingular. The step diagnostic is satisfied when \(\sigma_k\le\tau_x\) for a prescribed \(\tau_x\ge0\). This condition reports that the accepted iterate displacement is small in the chosen scaling. By itself it is not a convergence certificate: a small step may result from an active trust-region bound, restrictive line search, poor scaling, inaccurate derivatives, or finite-precision stagnation.
assumptions_latex: The same norm and scaling are used throughout the test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_k\le\tau_x\) identifies a small accepted step but is insufficient for convergence by itself.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled small-step test for detecting negligible iterate displacement.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The small-step diagnostic is mathematically coherent, but the specific normalization and its interpretation as the terminal diagnostic have no cited source. An authoritative stopping-test locator is required to establish the intended convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Agreement Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare actual and predicted merit reduction through their ratio; values near one indicate agreement, while nonpositive prediction invalidates the ratio test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\), and let \(m_k(s)\) be a local model with \(m_k(0)=\phi(x_k)\). For a trial step \(s_k\), define \[\operatorname{ared}_k=\phi(x_k)-\phi(x_k+s_k),\qquad \operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k).\] When \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\), the model-agreement ratio is \(\rho_k=\operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\). Values near one indicate accurate reduction prediction, \(\rho_k\le0\) indicates no realized decrease, and the ratio is diagnostically undefined when \(\operatorname{pred}_k\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\), \(\rho_k\) quantifies model agreement; otherwise the ratio is not a valid agreement diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Actual-to-predicted reduction test for a residual merit model.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Least-Squares Problems and Projections p. 68

knowledge_statements.title: Step–Model Consistency
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The step, model prediction, feasibility bound, and actual reduction must use the same base point, scaling, and trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trial step \(s_k\) and model \(m_k\) are step-model consistent when all quantities are evaluated at the same base point \(x_k\), with the same scaling and constraints, and \[m_k(0)=\phi(x_k),\qquad \operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0.\] If a trust-region radius \(\Delta_k\) is imposed in the scaled norm, consistency additionally requires \(\|D_xs_k\|\le\Delta_k\). The reported agreement ratio must then use the identical \(s_k\): \[\rho_k=\frac{\phi(x_k)-\phi(x_k+s_k)}{\operatorname{pred}_k}.\] Violation makes the step and agreement diagnostics incomparable.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\), \(s_k\), and \(\phi\) are finite at every displayed argument.
A trust-region constraint is included only when the solver imposes one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed identities and bound make the step diagnostic and model-agreement ratio mutually consistent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency checks coupling a computed step to its reported model prediction.

notation.meaning: Local merit model at iteration k.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The identities form a plausible solver-interface consistency rule, but no source supports the claimed required coupling among base point, scaling, constraints, prediction, and agreement ratio. The exact condition is therefore not independently reliable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-difference validation of a supplied Jacobian
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(\widetilde J(x)\) be a supplied Jacobian, and let \(e_j\) denote the \(j\)-th coordinate vector. Choose nonzero perturbations \(h_j\) and positive absolute and relative tolerances \(a_J,r_J\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic mappings evaluated in finite precision; validation is local at selected test points and directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the forward-difference column \(d_j(h_j)=[F(x+h_je_j)-F(x)]/h_j\) and the normalized discrepancy \(E_j=\|d_j(h_j)-\widetilde J(x)e_j\|/[a_J+r_J\max\{\|d_j(h_j)\|,\|\widetilde J(x)e_j\|\}]\). The supplied Jacobian passes the coordinate validation test at \(x\) when \(E_j\le1\) for every tested \(j\). A multiscale test evaluates several decreasing \(|h_j|\): truncation-dominated discrepancies should initially decrease, whereas eventual growth or stagnation is permitted once cancellation and function noise dominate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate each tested Jacobian column by a forward difference and compare it with the corresponding supplied column using mixed absolute and relative tolerances. The Jacobian passes when every normalized discrepancy is at most one. Repeating the comparison over several step sizes separates the initial truncation-error regime from the small-step regime dominated by cancellation or evaluation noise.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A directional variant replaces \(e_j\) by a nonzero test direction \(v\) and compares \([F(x+hv)-F(x)]/h\) with \(\widetilde J(x)v\).
For a scalar objective, the same test validates a supplied gradient through directional derivatives.
special_cases_latex: With exact arithmetic and Lipschitz Jacobian, forward-difference truncation error is \(O(|h_j|)\).
Central differences may be substituted when additional evaluations are affordable and greater truncation accuracy is desired.
immediate_consequences_latex: A failed column identifies variables associated with a derivative inconsistency.
Validation at the initial point can detect incorrectly coded analytic derivatives before nonlinear iteration.
boundary_notes: Agreement with finite differences is not a global correctness certificate.
Steps that are too small may produce misleading discrepancies through cancellation.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Test Problems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear test problem packages a residual map, domain, start, reference solutions, and independent oracle data; families may vary dimension and difficulty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear residual test problem is a tuple \(\mathcal{T}=(F,\mathcal{D},x_0,\mathcal{S},\mathcal{O})\), where \(F:\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\), \(x_0\in\mathcal{D}\) is a starting point, \(\mathcal{S}\) contains declared solutions or reference stationary points when known, and \(\mathcal{O}\) supplies independently specified residual or derivative reference data. A parameterized family \(\{\mathcal{T}_{\theta}\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\) is dimensionally scalable when \(n\) or \(m\) varies with \(\theta\), and structurally scalable when sparsity, conditioning, rank, or residual attainability can be varied independently.
assumptions_latex: Every declared evaluation point lies in \(\mathcal{D}\).
Reference data in \(\mathcal{O}\) are generated independently of the implementation under test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{T}\) supplies a reproducible instance for residual, derivative, and solver validation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized test instances for validating residual and derivative implementations.

notation.meaning: Declared reference solution or stationary-point data.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The proposed tuple is an interface-specific formalization rather than a standard definition established by the cited general chapter locator. In particular, mandatory independent oracle data and the two scalability classifications require direct source support.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative Checks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare claimed Jacobian-vector products with centered directional differences over several directions and step sizes, reporting normalized errors and invalid perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a residual implementation \(F:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\), a claimed Jacobian action \(v\mapsto\widehat J(x)v\), a point \(x\), nonzero directions \(v_1,\ldots,v_r\), and steps \(h_0>\cdots>h_L>0\). For each \((i,\ell)\), compute \[d_{i\ell}=\frac{F(x+h_\ell v_i)-F(x-h_\ell v_i)}{2h_\ell},\qquad e_{i\ell}=\frac{\|d_{i\ell}-\widehat J(x)v_i\|}{\max\{1,\|d_{i\ell}\|,\|\widehat J(x)v_i\|\}}.\] Report all \(e_{i\ell}\), the minimizing step for each direction, and failure if no interior step exhibits decreasing error before rounding error dominates. Domain-invalid perturbations are skipped and reported.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is evaluable at every unskipped perturbation.
Residual and claimed derivative evaluations use the same arithmetic and scaling conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The error table diagnoses directional inconsistency between \(F\) and \(\widehat J\); it does not prove global derivative correctness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional finite-difference validation of an implemented Jacobian action.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Centered directional differencing is standard, but the complete algorithm, normalization, interior-step requirement, and failure declaration have no citation. Moreover, 'exhibits decreasing error before rounding error dominates' lacks a quantitative decision rule, making the reported failure condition implementation-dependent.

knowledge_statements.title: Test-Coverage Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validation must span dimension, rank, conditioning, residual attainability, structure, location, direction, and step scale; success in one regime does not transfer automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative-validation suite has structural coverage only if its test set includes, whenever applicable: square, overdetermined, and underdetermined dimensions; zero and nonzero attainable residuals; full-rank and rank-deficient Jacobians; well- and ill-conditioned scalings; dense, sparse, block, and matrix-free interfaces; and points both near and away from solutions. For each regime, checks must exercise multiple coordinate and noncoordinate directions and at least two admissible step scales. Passing one regime does not imply correctness in another because rank, scaling, sparsity, boundary feasibility, and residual attainability change the observable failure modes.
assumptions_latex: Only regimes supported by the declared solver interface are required.
Expected structural properties of each test instance are independently documented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coverage requires representative tests across every applicable structural regime and cannot be inferred from a single problem class.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage requirements for residual, Jacobian, and solver-interface validation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The coverage dimensions are plausible engineering recommendations, but the universal 'only if' claim and mandatory direction and step-scale counts are not supported by evidence. A source or a clearly established local validation standard is needed for these requirements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disjoint classification of unsuccessful nonlinear-solver termination
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\) be the final iterate of a nonlinear-equation or minimization solver. Let \(R_k\) be its scaled residual, \(G_k\) its scaled stationarity measure, \(S_k\) its relative-step measure, and let \(L_k\) encode exhausted iteration or evaluation limits. Choose positive tolerances \(\varepsilon_R,\varepsilon_G,\varepsilon_S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic solvers; failure labels apply only after the relevant success tests have failed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Termination failure discrimination is the ordered classification: nonroot stationary termination when \(R_k>\varepsilon_R\) and \(G_k\le\varepsilon_G\); stagnation when \(R_k>\varepsilon_R\), \(G_k>\varepsilon_G\), and \(S_k\le\varepsilon_S\); resource exhaustion when no preceding label applies and \(L_k=1\); divergence when no preceding label applies and a prescribed divergence condition holds; otherwise unresolved failure. For nonlinear equations, the first class identifies approximate stationarity of \(\tfrac12\|D_FF(x)\|_2^2\) at a point whose residual is not acceptably small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After ruling out successful convergence, classify termination in a fixed order. A small gradient of the residual merit function with a non-small residual is a nonroot stationary failure. A tiny step with neither residual nor stationarity success is stagnation. Exhausted budgets and detected divergence receive separate labels. Anything not meeting these conditions remains unresolved rather than being reported as convergence.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|D_FF(x)\|_2^2\), the nonroot stationary condition uses \(\nabla\phi(x)=J(x)^TD_F^TD_FF(x)\approx0\) together with \(D_FF(x)\not\approx0\).
special_cases_latex: An iteration limit reached at an otherwise successful root remains successful because success tests precede failure labels.
Repeated maximum-length steps may instantiate the divergence indicator \(\mathcal V_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A solver cannot label a nonroot local minimizer of the residual merit function as a root.
Stagnation is separated from insufficient computational budget.
boundary_notes: The classification diagnoses observed termination and does not identify every underlying cause.
Inaccurate derivatives, poor scaling, or finite-precision limits may each produce the same stagnation label.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation Detection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Declare stagnation only after a window of negligible merit change and scaled steps while convergence tests remain unsatisfied; treat it as failure, not success.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a window length \(w\ge1\), progress tolerance \(\tau_p\ge0\), and step tolerance \(\tau_x\ge0\). For merit function \(\phi\), declare stagnation at iteration \(k\ge w\) when no convergence certificate holds and \[\max_{j=k-w,\ldots,k-1}\frac{|\phi(x_{j+1})-\phi(x_j)|}{1+|\phi(x_j)|}\le\tau_p,\qquad \max_{j=k-w,\ldots,k-1}\frac{\|D_x(x_{j+1}-x_j)\|}{1+\|D_xx_j\|}\le\tau_x.\] The declaration is a failure diagnostic, not successful termination: it records persistent negligible progress and requires separate discrimination among rounding limits, poor scaling, inaccurate derivatives, globalization restrictions, and genuine near-stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi(x_j)\) and \(x_j\) are finite throughout the window.
\(D_x\) and the diagnostic tolerances remain fixed over the window.
At least one declared convergence certificate is evaluated independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two windowed inequalities, together with failed convergence tests, diagnose stagnation without identifying its cause.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed detection of negligible progress without satisfaction of convergence tests.

notation.meaning: Number of consecutive transitions in the diagnostic window.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The windowed criterion is internally coherent and correctly classified as a failure diagnostic, but its conjunction of merit-change and step tests, normalizations, window length, and tolerances is a policy choice with no supplied source. The exact stagnation condition therefore requires authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.title: False-Convergence Detection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Declare false convergence when a solver reports success from a small step even though the scaled residual, or another required acceptance measure, still exceeds tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(x_k\) be the current iterate, and let \(D_x,D_F\) be nonsingular scaling matrices. Define \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\). A step-based success declaration at iteration \(k+1\) is false convergence whenever
\[
\|D_xs_k\|\le \tau_x\bigl(1+\|D_xx_{k+1}\|\bigr)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\|D_FF(x_{k+1})\|>\tau_F.
\]
If an objective or merit reduction test is also required, its failure likewise prevents a success declaration. Thus a small step is evidence of negligible progress, not independently a certificate that \(F(x)=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(F(x_{k+1})\) and the accepted step \(s_k\) are computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|D_xs_k\|\le \tau_x(1+\|D_xx_{k+1}\|)\) and \(\|D_FF(x_{k+1})\|>\tau_F\) imply that step-based success is false convergence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic predicate for rejecting step-based success when the nonlinear residual remains unacceptably large.

notation.meaning: accepted displacement from iteration k to k+1

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the false-convergence leaf and is internally coherent, but the precise scaled-step and residual thresholds are solver-dependent. No inspectable source with a section, theorem, or page locator supports this particular diagnostic rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation–Termination Discrimination
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual satisfaction means successful termination; persistently tiny steps with inadequate residual reduction mean stagnation; otherwise neither outcome follows from these tests alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a window length \(q\ge 1\), define scaled residuals \(\rho_j=\|D_FF(x_j)\|\) and scaled steps \(\sigma_j=\|D_x(x_{j+1}-x_j)\|/(1+\|D_xx_{j+1}\|)\). Successful termination at \(x_k\) requires \(\rho_k\le\tau_F\). If instead
\[
\rho_k>\tau_F,\qquad
\max_{k-q\le j<k}\sigma_j\le\tau_x,
\qquad
\rho_k\ge(1-\tau_p)\rho_{k-q},
\]
then the appropriate outcome is stagnation rather than convergence. When neither predicate holds, iteration should continue unless another failure or resource-limit test applies.
assumptions_latex: The same fixed scalings \(D_x,D_F\) are used throughout the monitoring window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual test certifies termination, whereas the displayed small-step and insufficient-progress tests classify the outcome as stagnation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision rule separating successful residual termination from unsuccessful stagnation over a finite monitoring window.

notation.meaning: scaled residual norm at iteration j
relative scaled step at iteration j

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The record fits stagnation–termination discrimination, but the finite-window predicate and the factor 1−tau_p are specific design choices rather than source-independent definitions. An authoritative locator supporting these hypotheses and classification thresholds is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical Verification and Performance Descriptor
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be a residual map, let \(x_k\) be iterates produced by a numerical solver, and let \(x_*\) denote an exact solution when one exists. Let \(r_k=F(x_k)\), let \(J_k\) denote an exact or computed Jacobian, and let \(W_k\) be the accumulated computational work.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic residual solvers are considered. The definition organizes reported evidence; it does not assert that a small residual proves the existence or uniqueness of a nearby root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A numerical verification-performance descriptor is a tuple \(\mathcal{V}_k=(E_k,C_k,R_k,W_k)\). Here \(E_k\) is numerical evidence, containing computable quantities such as \(\|r_k\|\), step norms, and stopping-test values; \(C_k\) is a rigorous certificate whose predicates may assert existence, uniqueness, or exclusion of roots in a specified set; \(R_k\) is a conditioning and convergence descriptor containing quantities such as \(\kappa(J_k)\), forward- or backward-error bounds, and an asymptotic rate class; and \(W_k\) is a work vector counting separately residual evaluations, Jacobian evaluations, factorizations, linear solves, iterations, and storage. Two solver reports are comparable under this taxonomy only after their norms, tolerances, certificate predicates, and work units have been identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numerical verification-performance descriptor separates four kinds of information: computed numerical evidence, logically rigorous root certificates, conditioning and convergence information, and computational work. A report is comparable with another report only when the norms, tolerances, certificate meanings, and counted work units are stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{V}_k=(E_k,C_k,R_k,W_k)\), with numerical evidence, rigorous certificates, conditioning/rate descriptors, and work counts represented as distinct components.
special_cases_latex: When no validated enclosure is computed, \(C_k\) is empty even if \(\|F(x_k)\|\) is small.
For a derivative-free method, the Jacobian-evaluation component of \(W_k\) is zero, while residual evaluations used to build models remain in the residual count.
immediate_consequences_latex: A residual norm and a root-existence certificate are not interchangeable fields.
Iteration counts alone do not determine work unless the per-iteration operations are fixed.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a particular stopping tolerance or scalar aggregation of the work vector.
The inspected sources discuss several constituent measures but do not state this exact four-part taxonomy.

notation.meaning: computable numerical evidence at iteration k

review_flags: No inspected source states the exact combined taxonomy, particularly its separation of numerical evidence from rigorous root validation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioning–Backward–Forward Error Certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(x=A^{-1}b\), and let \(\widehat{x}\) be a computed approximation. Fix a subordinate matrix norm and its associated vector norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the finite-dimensional linearized certificate underlying residual-system error assessment. Nonlinear use requires a justified local linearization or an independent nonlinear remainder bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conditioning-error certificate for \(A\widehat{x}\approx b\) is a tuple \((\eta,\kappa,\varepsilon_f)\) in which the normwise relative backward error is \(\eta=\inf\{\epsilon\geq0:\exists\,\Delta A,\Delta b,\ (A+\Delta A)\widehat{x}=b+\Delta b,\ \|\Delta A\|\leq\epsilon\|A\|,\ \|\Delta b\|\leq\epsilon\|b\|\}\), the condition number is \(\kappa(A)=\|A\|\|A^{-1}\|\), and \(\varepsilon_f\) is a certified upper bound on \(\|x-\widehat{x}\|/\|x\|\). The certificate is condition-guided when its forward component is obtained from a valid perturbation inequality, for example \(\varepsilon_f\leq \kappa(A)\eta/(1-\kappa(A)\eta)\) whenever the adopted perturbation model yields this bound and \(\kappa(A)\eta<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate records three distinct quantities: the smallest relative perturbation that makes the computed vector exact, the condition number of the problem, and a valid relative forward-error bound. A small backward error implies a small forward error only when the condition number is moderate enough for the applicable perturbation bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta\) measures backward error, \(\kappa(A)=\|A\|\|A^{-1}\|\) measures sensitivity, and \(\varepsilon_f\) bounds the resulting forward error under the stated perturbation regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If only the right-hand side is perturbed, then \(\eta_b=\|b-A\widehat{x}\|/\|b\|\) is the relative backward error for that restricted model.
special_cases_latex: For \(A=J_F(\widehat{x})\), the tuple describes the conditioning of a Newton correction equation rather than, by itself, the full nonlinear root error.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\kappa(A)\eta\) is not small, backward stability alone does not certify forward accuracy.
A singular \(A\) has infinite normwise condition number under this convention.
boundary_notes: Componentwise backward errors require componentwise perturbation sets and can differ substantially from the normwise quantity.
The rational forward bound depends on the precise perturbation model; it must not be applied when its hypotheses fail.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Root Sensitivity Induced by the Jacobian
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable near \((x_*,\theta_*)\), with \(F(x_*,\theta_*)=0\). Write \(J_*=D_xF(x_*,\theta_*)\) and \(B_*=D_\theta F(x_*,\theta_*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns a regular isolated root of a smooth square system. Singular roots, set-valued solution maps, and nonsmooth generalized derivatives are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The root and Jacobian are regularly sensitivity-coupled at \((x_*,\theta_*)\) when \(J_*\) is nonsingular and the local solution branch \(x(\theta)\), defined by \(F(x(\theta),\theta)=0\) and \(x(\theta_*)=x_*\), has first-order sensitivity operator \(S_*=-J_*^{-1}B_*\). Its absolute local condition number is \(\chi_{\mathrm{abs}}=\|S_*\|\). When \(x_*\neq0\) and \(\theta_*\neq0\), the corresponding relative condition number is \(\chi_{\mathrm{rel}}=(\|\theta_*\|/\|x_*\|)\|S_*\|\). For an additive residual perturbation \(F(x,\theta_*)+d=0\), one has \(B_*=I\) in the perturbation variable and the first-order root displacement is governed by \(-J_*^{-1}d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular root, parameter perturbations change the root to first order through the inverse root Jacobian multiplied by the parameter derivative of the residual. The induced operator norm is the absolute condition number, with a scaled version giving relative conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\theta x(\theta_*)=-J_*^{-1}D_\theta F(x_*,\theta_*)\), and its induced norm defines the local root-sensitivity measure.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For additive residual perturbations, \(\delta x=-J_*^{-1}d+o(\|d\|)\).
special_cases_latex: For a scalar equation, the absolute sensitivity to additive residual perturbations is \(1/|F'(x_*)|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A nearly singular \(J_*\) can amplify small residual or data perturbations into large root changes.
The matrix condition number \(\|J_*\|\|J_*^{-1}\|\) and the root condition number \(\|J_*^{-1}B_*\|\) answer related but different scaling questions.
boundary_notes: The formulas are local and first order; they are not global forward-error certificates.
No inspected source in the supplied locator set states the full parameterized-root definition with these exact quantifiers.

notation.meaning: Jacobian with respect to the root variable at the reference root
derivative of the residual with respect to parameters

knowledge_statements.title: Local Root Sensitivity Induced by the Jacobian
Root Conditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple root amplifies small additive residual perturbations to first order by the inverse Jacobian; its absolute condition number is the inverse-Jacobian operator norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable near a root \(x_*\), with \(J_*=F'(x_*)\) nonsingular. For perturbed equations \(F(x)+h=0\), the local root map \(x(h)\) satisfies
\[
x(h)-x_*=-J_*^{-1}h+o(\|h\|).
\]
Relative to specified norms on residual and variable space, the absolute root condition number is
\[
\kappa_{\mathrm{root}}(x_*)=
\sup_{h\ne0}\frac{\|J_*^{-1}h\|}{\|h\|}
=\|J_*^{-1}\|.
\]
A scaled condition number is obtained by replacing \(J_*^{-1}\) with \(D_xJ_*^{-1}D_F^{-1}\).
assumptions_latex: All vector and induced operator norms are fixed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute first-order conditioning of a simple square-system root under additive residual perturbations.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of F at the root
additive perturbation of the residual equation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: implicit-function characterization of simple-root conditioning

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The simple-root perturbation formula and inverse-Jacobian condition number are mathematically standard and match the leaf, but no source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first-order change in a Newton step is the inverse Jacobian applied to residual error plus the Jacobian perturbation acting on the original step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the Newton correction \(s\) solve \(Js=-r\), where \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular. If \(J\) and \(r\) receive perturbations \(E\) and \(e\), and \(J+E\) remains nonsingular, then the perturbed correction \(s+\delta s\) obeys
\[
\delta s=-J^{-1}(e+Es)+\mathcal{O}\bigl((\|E\|+\|e\|)^2\bigr).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\|\delta s\|\le \|J^{-1}\|\bigl(\|e\|+\|E\|\,\|s\|\bigr)+\mathcal{O}\bigl((\|E\|+\|e\|)^2\bigr).
\]
Thus near-singularity of \(J\) amplifies both residual and Jacobian errors in the computed correction.
assumptions_latex: Perturbations \(E,e\) tend jointly to zero and are small enough that \(J+E\) remains nonsingular.
A compatible vector norm and induced matrix norm are used.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order dependence of a Newton correction on perturbations in its Jacobian and residual data.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: first-order perturbation of a nonsingular linear solve

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning–Sensitivity Coupling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameter sensitivity of a simple root equals the inverse root Jacobian times residual parameter sensitivity, so poor root conditioning amplifies parameter effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable near \((x_*,p_*)\), with \(F(x_*,p_*)=0\) and \(J_x=F_x(x_*,p_*)\) nonsingular. Then the locally unique root branch \(x(p)\) is differentiable at \(p_*\) and
\[
D_px(p_*)=-J_x^{-1}F_p(x_*,p_*).
\]
Hence, for compatible induced norms,
\[
\|D_px(p_*)\|\le \|J_x^{-1}\|\,\|F_p(x_*,p_*)\|.
\]
The inverse-Jacobian root condition factor therefore multiplies the sensitivity of the residual equations to parameter changes.
assumptions_latex: Compatible norms are fixed on parameter, residual, and variable spaces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit-function coupling between parameter sensitivity and inverse-Jacobian root conditioning.

notation.meaning: Jacobian with respect to the root variable
Jacobian of the residual with respect to parameters
derivative of the local root branch

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
